source.title: The universal p-adic Gross–Zagier formula
readSections: Read in full in arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024), whose abstract page carries the comment "89 pages, 1 figure. New in this version: a correction as Appendix B (to appear separately in Invent. math.)" and the journal reference Invent. math. 230 (2022), 509–649: §1 Introduction and statements of the main results; §2 Automorphic and Galois representations; §3 Sheaves on Hida families; §4 Pairings; §5 Selmer sheaves and p-adic heights; §6 Universal Heegner class; §7 The main theorems, and a conjecture; Appendix A p-adic semilocal constructions; Appendix B Correction; and the bibliography.

Sources read: the arXiv e-print archive of v4, sha256 24d867874a39fd374d8820069c76e972d9260b7bc6b0b5617e2bafdcc86d330c, whose main file univ-corr-arxiv.tex (6803 lines, sha256 ca60c39e761b3e5b5dd0d4c6423c0eba4703b9065850ce5909a95b58d7399f2e) uses smfart.cls with smfenum.sty, smfhyperref.sty and smfthm.sty; and the compiled PDF of v4, sha256 c50d0cd394a5e803c0b7adef5700b425f4f304679415b2c666cd351eefcd9602.

Numbering: the SMF class numbers theo/prop/conj/coro/lemm/defi/rema/exem and the enonce environment on a single counter within each subsection, with a separate equation counter also within subsection; the lettered theoA environment is numbered A–H and the customthm/customconj environments carry the manual labels B^ord and Pf. The numbering was re-derived from the LaTeX and checked against all 68 typed cross-references printed in the PDF: 107 numbered statements (37 Lemmas, 26 Propositions, 15 Remarks, 12 Definitions, 8 lettered Theorems, 4 Theorems, 4 Corollaries, 1 Construction), with the two apparent mismatches explained (one is an external citation to Howard, the other is the misprint recorded as E2 below).

summary: Disegni proves a p-adic Gross–Zagier formula in three linked forms and deduces arithmetic consequences. Fix a prime p, a totally real field F, a CM quadratic extension E/F, an incoherent totally definite quaternion algebra B over F_A split at p, and the groups G, H = Res_{E/Q}G_m, (G×H)' = (G×H)/Z with their towers of quaternionic Shimura curves X, Y, Z and the diagonal embedding e' : Y' → Z. For an ordinary, locally distinguished automorphic representation Π = π ⊗ χ of (G×H)'(A) of cohomological weight W over a p-adic field, the Abel–Jacobi images of the CM 0-cycles with coefficients in the local system attached to W give a functional P_Π : Π → H^1(E,V_Π). Theorem B computes the p-adic height of P_Π ⊗ P_{Π^∨} against the automorphic inner product as the derivative at s = 0 of the cyclotomic p-adic L-function of V_{(π,χ)}, times an explicit interpolation factor and the normalised product of local toric integrals Q. Theorem C constructs a universal Heegner class 𝓟 over a locally distinguished Hida family X for (G×H)', valued in a sheaf of Nekovář Selmer groups, and proves that it specialises to the Heegner classes at every classical point, answering the generalisation of a question of Howard. Theorem D is the interpolated formula over X, an identity between the height of 𝓟 and the normal derivative of the two-variable p-adic L-function; Theorem B for all weights is deduced from it by density of the trivial-weight points where the formula is known and by multiplicity one. The applications are the p-adic Beilinson–Bloch–Kato conjecture in analytic rank one (Theorem A), an Iwasawa main conjecture for derivatives (Theorem E), the generic non-vanishing of p-adic heights on self-dual CM motives (Theorem F) and along an exceptional classical Hida family (Theorem G), a universal Waldspurger formula for coherent totally definite quaternion algebras (Theorem H), a conjecture à la Bertolini–Darmon for the leading term of 𝓟 in terms of Pfaffian height regulators, and a new proof of the theorem of Greenberg–Stevens. The technical core is Appendix A, which constructs semilocal operators at p∞ intertwining ordinary, anti-ordinary and toric parts of a locally algebraic representation and computes the local toric periods of the resulting vectors in terms of Deligne–Langlands gamma factors. The paper needs: Hida theory for the four groups and their eigenvarieties; the Galois representations of Hilbert modular forms with local–global compatibility and the nearly ordinary filtration; pseudocharacters and Azumaya algebras over an eigenvariety; the local Langlands correspondence in analytic families; Nekovář's Selmer complexes and height pairings in families, with Venerucci's conormal refinement; the étale Abel–Jacobi map for 0-cycles with coefficients; Saito–Tunnell multiplicity one and the local toric integrals of Waldspurger; the two-variable p-adic L-function of Disegni's companion paper; the Euler system bounds of Fouquet; and, for the applications, Katz's p-adic L-function, Hsieh's μ-invariant theorem, Hida's anticyclotomic main conjecture and the Bertolini–Darmon rigid-analytic formula. Appendix B of arXiv v4 is a published Correction, to appear separately in Inventiones: after a correction to Disegni's companion paper on nonsplit primes, Theorems A, B and B^ord hold only under the extra condition (★) — every p-adic place of F nonsplit in E is inert and χ is unramified there — and Theorems D and E hold for Hida* families rather than Hida families. Every item below states the corrected form.

items.name: Incoherent reductive group over a global field
items.statement: An F-incoherent reductive group G over a global field F is a collection of reductive groups G_v/F_v, one for each place v, such that for every place w there is a genuine reductive group G(w)/F with G(w)×_F F_v ≅ G_v for all v ≠ w and with G(w)×_F F_w and G_w non-isomorphic inner forms of each other. For a finite extension F/F_0, an F-incoherent reductive group over F_0 is a collection G_{v_0}/F_{0,v_0} of the form Res_{F_{v_0}/F_{0,v_0}} G_{F,v_0} for an F-incoherent group G_F over F; one writes G = Res_{F/F_0} G_F. All but finitely many G_{v_0} are unramified, so the restricted product G(A^S) is defined; when F_0 = Q and G_{F,∞} is anisotropic modulo its centre one redefines G(A^S) := G(A^{S∞}) × G_∞ with G_∞ = G_p(Q_p) carrying the Zariski topology.
items.locator: §2.1.1 (Incoherent reductive groups), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The incoherent quaternionic group, its companions, and the embedding e
items.statement: B is a quaternion algebra over F_A with ramification set Σ ⊔ {v | ∞} satisfying |Σ| ≡ [F:Q] − 1 (mod 2); G(A) := B^× is the incoherent group over Q with G_v = B_v^×. With H := Res_{E/Q}G_m and Z := Res_{F/Q}G_m one considers the five groups G, H, G×H, (G×H)' := (G×H)/Z and H' := H/Z, written collectively G_*. If E_v/F_v is nonsplit for every v ∈ Σ there is a unique B^×-conjugacy class of F_A-embeddings E_A ↪ B; fixing one gives e : H ↪ G and a diagonal H' ↪ (G×H)'.
items.locator: §1.2.1 (Algebraic groups and Shimura varieties), display (1.2.1), and §2.1.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Hecke algebras of a coherent or incoherent group and the involution ι
items.statement: For a ring A, 𝓗_{G,A} := C_c^∞(G(A^{p∞}),A) and 𝓗^S_{G,A} := C_c^∞(G(A^{Sp∞}),A), with bi-U-invariant subalgebras 𝓗_{G,U,A}, 𝓗^S_{G,U,A}; S is U-spherical when U_v is maximal for v ∉ S. For a smooth A-module M the spherical Hecke algebra acting on M is 𝓗^{sph}_G := lim_{(S,U)} 𝓗^S_{G,U}(M) ⊂ End_A(M) when the limit over U-spherical pairs stabilises. It carries the involution ι induced by g ↦ g^{T,−1} on G and h ↦ h^{−1} on H, and on the torus by t ↦ t ν(t)^{−1}, ν the reduced norm (for G) or N_{E/F} (for H); ι preserves T^+_{G_*}.
items.locator: §2.1.2 (Hecke algebras) and §2.1.4 (Involutions), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Congruence subgroups at p and the semigroup T^+
items.statement: For v | p: U^1_1(ϖ_v^r) = {(a b; c d) ∈ GL_2(O_{F,v}) : a−1 ≡ d−1 ≡ c ≡ 0 mod ϖ_v^r} and U(ϖ_v^r) the further condition b ≡ 0. With ε_v ∈ F_v^× such that E_v = F_v(√ε_v) and v(ε_v) ≥ 1, V_{v,r} := V_{F,v,r}(1+ϖ^r O_{E,w}) in the split case and V_{F,v,r}(1+√ε_v ϖ^r O_{E,w}) in the nonsplit case, U_{v,r} := U^1_1(ϖ_v^{r}); K_{p,r} and K_p(p^{r}) are the images of U_{p,r}×V_{p,r} and U_p(p^{r})×V_{p,r} in (G×H)'. N_{G,0} is the unipotent upper-triangular integral subgroup, T_{G_*} the diagonal torus, T^+_{G_*} the normaliser of N_{G_*,0} in T_{G_*}, so that T^+_{G,v} = {diag(t_1,t_2) : v(t_1) ≥ v(t_2)}.
items.locator: §2.1.3 (Subgroups of G_*) and §2.1.5 (Congruence subgroups), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Highest-weight character of an algebraic representation and its dual
items.statement: For an irreducible left (resp. right) algebraic representation W of G_* over L, σ_W is the character by which T_{G_*} acts on the line W^{N_{G_*}} of highest-weight vectors (resp. on W_{N_{G_*}}). One has σ_{W^∨}(t) = σ_W(t^ι) for the involution t ↦ t ν(t)^{−1}.
items.locator: §2.2.1 (Highest-weight character), display (2.2.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Cohomological weights and algebraic representations of the quaternionic group
items.statement: A cohomological weight for G over L is a tuple w̲ = (w; (w_σ)_{σ: F ↪ L}) of [F:Q]+1 integers of the same parity with w_σ ≥ 2. The associated representation is W_{G,w̲} := ⊗_{σ} Sym^{w_σ−2} Std_σ ⊗ Nm_σ^{(w−w_σ+2)/2}, with dual W_{G,w̲^∨}, w̲^∨ = (−w;(w_σ)). Concretely W_{G,w̲} is the space of tuples of homogeneous polynomials p_σ ∈ L[x_σ,y_σ] of degree w_σ−2 with g·p_σ(x,y) = det(σg)^{(w−w_σ+2)/2} p_σ((x,y)σg); it carries the O_L-lattice of tuples with integral coefficients. Then σ_{W,v}(diag(t_1,t_2)) = ∏_{σ: F_v ↪ L} σ(t_1)^{(w+w_σ−2)/2} σ(t_2)^{(w−w_σ+2)/2}. If L/Q_p is Galois, W_{G,w̲} descends to the fixed field L(w̲) of the stabiliser of w̲.
items.locator: §2.2.2 (Quaternionic special case), displays (2.2.2)–(2.2.5), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Cohomological weights and algebraic characters of the torus H
items.statement: A cohomological weight for H is a tuple l̲ = (l;(l_σ)_{σ: F ↪ L}) of [F:Q]+1 integers of the same parity; after choosing an extension σ' of each σ to E, W_{H,l̲} := ⊗_σ σ'^{l_σ} ⊗ σ∘Nm_{E_p/F_p}^{(l−l_σ)/2}, a one-dimensional L-space with E_p^×-action, with an O_{E,p}^×-stable lattice.
items.locator: §2.2.3 (Toric special case), display (2.2.6), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The Shimura data and the towers X, Y, X×Y, Z, Y'
items.statement: For an infinite place τ of F let G_τ = Res_{F/Q}G_F(τ) be the τ-nearby coherent group and h_{G,τ} : S = Res_{C/R}G_m → G_R Carayol's Hodge cocharacter; h_H is the unique cocharacter with e_R ∘ h_H = h_G. Products and projections give Shimura data for all five groups, hence towers X_{*,τ}/τE_* with reflex field E_* = E except E_G = F, and these descend to towers X_*/E_*: X/F, Y/E, X×_F Y/E, Z/E, Y'/E, the first three of dimension one and Y, Y' of dimension zero. Complex uniformisations: X_{U,τ}(C) ≅ B(τ)^× \ 𝔥^± × B^{∞×}/U ∪ {cusps}, Y_V(E^{ab}) ≅ E^× \ E_{A^∞}^×/V, and Z_K ≅ X_U × Y_V/Δ_{U,V}.
items.locator: §2.3.1 (Shimura varieties), displays (1.2.2) and (2.3.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)
items.note: The coherent quaternionic Shimura curves and their canonical models are planned by ShimuraVarieties V1/V8 and by HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.1; ShimuraData D4 plans data and morphisms. What is not planned is the incoherent case — the τ-nearby groups and the compatible system of towers attached to an incoherent G — which is the separate item incoherent-group.

items.name: Free action at sufficiently small level and the étale covering
items.statement: Lemma 2.3.1. If U_*^p is sufficiently small (independently of n) then (1) Ḡ_n := U_{*,p}/U_{*,p,n}(Z_{G_*}(Q) ∩ U_*)_p acts freely on X_{U_*^p U_{*,p,n}}, so that X_{*,U_*^pU_{*,p,n}} → X_{*,U_*} is étale with Galois group Ḡ_{*,n}; (2) Z_{G_*}(Q) ∩ U_* acts trivially on the lattice W^∘.
items.locator: Lemma 2.3.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (proof: Carayol, Lemme 1.4.1.1, plus the cohomological-weight condition)
items.note: H3 plans the arithmetic quotient and unit actions and R18.1 the quaternionic moduli; the neatness statement and the triviality of the action of the global units of cohomological weight are exactly what those layers must supply.

items.name: Automorphic étale local systems on the Shimura tower
items.statement: For an irreducible right algebraic representation W of G_* over L, a sufficiently small U_*, a U_{*,p}-stable lattice W^∘ and U_{*,p,n} acting trivially on W^∘/p^n, the quotient (X_{*,U_*^pU_{*,p,n}} × W^∘/p^n)/Ḡ_{*,n} is a locally constant étale O_L/p^n-module 𝓦^n on X_{*,U_*}; 𝓦^∘ := lim_n 𝓦^n and 𝓦 := 𝓦^∘ ⊗ L. 𝓦 is compatible with pullback in the tower and independent of W^∘ up to isomorphism; for a noncompact X_* the construction is performed on the open part and pushed forward to the compactification.
items.locator: §2.3.2 (Automorphic local systems), display (2.3.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)
items.note: R18.4 plans étale and Betti cohomology with algebraic local systems on the Hilbert/quaternionic towers together with the integral Hecke modules; the construction of the local system from a lattice and a neat level is its input.

items.name: p-adic automorphic representation of weight W (Emerton's point of view)
items.statement: Definition 2.4.1. With G_*(A) redefined as G_*(A^∞) × G_{*,∞}, where G_{*,∞} = G_*(Q_p) with the Zariski topology, a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of G_*(A) over L of weight W is an irreducible admissible locally algebraic representation π factoring as π = π^∞ ⊗ W, with G_*(A^∞) acting smoothly and G_{*,∞} algebraically, occurring as a subrepresentation of 𝓗^•(X̄_*, 𝓦^∨) = colim_U H^•(X̄_{*,U},𝓦^∨) ⊗ W.
items.locator: Definition 2.4.1 with Remark 2.4.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Ordinary automorphic representation and its ordinary part
items.statement: Definition 2.4.3. π of weight W = W_{G_*,w̲} is ordinary at v | p with unit character α_v^∘ if there is a smooth character α_v of T_v with π_v the unique irreducible subrepresentation of Ind(α_v·(|·|_v,|·|_v^{−1})) and α_v^∘ := α_v σ_{W,v} : T_v → O_L^×; equivalently, for r large the U^1_1(ϖ_v^r)-fixed vectors of π_v ⊗ W contain a unique line of simultaneous eigenvectors for the U_x = [U^1_1(ϖ_v^r) diag(x,1) U^1_1(ϖ_v^r)] with eigenvalue α^∘(x). That line is π_v^{ord} := L w_v ⊗ W^{N_v}, and π^{ord} := π^{p∞} ⊗ ⊗_{v|p} π_v^{ord}, on which T^+ acts by U_t ↦ α^∘(t). π is ordinary if it is so at all v | p. All automorphic representations of H(A^∞) are ordinary by convention, and π ⊗ χ is ordinary if π and χ are.
items.locator: Definition 2.4.3 with displays (2.4.1)–(2.4.3), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Galois representations attached to Hilbert modular forms (Ohta–Carayol–Saito)
items.statement: Theorem 2.5.1. For π of weight W over L and S ⊇ {ramified places} ∪ {v | p} there is a 2-dimensional absolutely irreducible ρ_π : G_{F,S} → Aut(V_π) with Tr ρ(Fr_v) = q_v^{−1} λ_{π_v}(T_v) for v ∉ S, and: (1) ρ_v is unramified for almost all v, potentially semistable for v | p, and the attached Weil–Deligne representation r_v matches π_v under local Langlands normalised à la Hecke, L(s,r_v) = L(s+1/2,π_v); (2) r_v satisfies weight–monodromy, its monodromy filtration being pure of weight w−1, and the filtration is trivial iff π_v is not special; (3) ρ is odd at every archimedean place; (4) for v | p and σ : F_v ↪ L̄ the σ-Hodge–Tate weights of ρ_v ⊗ L̄ are −1−(w+w_σ−2)/2 and −(w−w_σ+2)/2, and if π is ordinary at v there is a unique exact sequence 0 → V^+_{π,v} → V_{π,v} → V^−_{π,v} → 0 of G_{F,v}-representations with both terms one-dimensional and G_{F,v} acting on V^+_{π,v} by α^∘_{π,v} χ_cyc,v.
items.locator: Theorem 2.5.1 with display (2.5.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Carayol; T. Saito, Theorems 2.2 and 2.4; Tian–Xiao, Proposition 6.7)
items.note: R19.2 plans Hilbert and quaternionic Galois representations, R19.4 local–global compatibility away from p and R19.5 compatibility at the coefficient prime, including Hodge–Tate weights and the nearly ordinary filtration.

items.name: Carayol's decomposition of the homology of the Shimura tower
items.statement: Proposition 2.5.2. For U_* ⊂ G_*(A^∞), an irreducible right algebraic W over L and a sufficiently large finite Galois L'/L there is a Gal(L'/L)-equivariant isomorphism of 𝓗_{G_*,U_*,L}[G_{E_*,S}]-modules 𝓗_d(X̄_{*,U_*},𝓦) ⊗_L L' ≅ ⊕_π π^{∨,U_*} ⊗ V_π, the sum over automorphic representations of G_*(A) of weight W over L'. Here G_{E_*} is redefined as G_F × G_E when G_* = G×H or (G×H)'.
items.locator: Proposition 2.5.2, display (2.5.3), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Carayol, Sur les représentations l-adiques…, for G_* = G; the general case follows with class field theory)
items.note: R18.4 plans the integral Hecke modules and pairings on the quaternionic cohomology and R19.2 the attached Galois representations; their joint content is the isotypic decomposition used here.

items.name: Weight space, the ordinary Iwasawa algebra and its classical points
items.statement: Definition 3.1.1. For U_*^p ⊂ G_*(A^{p∞}) set Z_{G_*,U^p_*} ⊂ Z_{G_*}(Q) as in the text, T̄_{G_*,U^p_*,0} := T_{G,0}/closure(Z_{G_*,U_*}) and Λ^∘_{G_*,U^p_*} := Z_p⟦T̄_{G_*,0}⟧. For an irreducible algebraic W, I_{G_*,U^p_*,W,r,L} := ([t] − σ_W^{−1}(t))_{t ∈ T̄_{G_*,U^p_*,r}}; these form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of 0, Λ^∘_{G_*,U^p_*,W,r} ≅ O_L[T̄_{G_*,U^p_*,0}/T̄_{G_*,U^p_*,r}] via [t] ↦ σ_W^{−1}(t)[t̄], and Λ_{G_*,U^p_*} = (lim_r Λ_{G_*,U^p_*,W,r}) ⊗ L. The weight space is 𝔚_{G_*,U^p_*} := Spec Λ_{G_*,U^p_*} ⊗ Q_p, with the zero-dimensional ind-subschemes 𝔚^{cl,W}_{·,r}, 𝔚^{cl,W}, 𝔚^{cl} of classical points. Writing T̄_{G_*,U^p_*,0} ≅ Δ × Z_p^{d(G_*)} one has d(G) = d(H) = [F:Q]+1+δ and d((G×H)') = 2[F:Q]+1+δ, δ = δ_{F,p} the Leopoldt defect of F at p.
items.locator: §3.1.1 (Weight spaces), Definition 3.1.1 with displays (3.1.1)–(3.1.3), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Ordinary completed homology of the Shimura tower
items.statement: For an irreducible right algebraic W with lattice W^∘, 𝓗_d(X̄_{*,U_*^pU_{*,r}},𝓦^∘)^{ord} := (H_d^{ét}(X̄_{*,U_*^pU_{*,r}},𝓦^∘) ⊗_{O_L[T^+_{G_*}]} (W^{∘,∨})_{N_0})^{ord} for the action of T^+_{G_*} by U_t ⊗ t, and M^∘_{G_*,U^p_*,W} := lim_r 𝓗_d(X̄_{*,U^p_*U_{*,p,r}},𝓦^∘)^{ord}, M_{G_*,U^p_*,W} := M^∘ ⊗_{O_L} L, which is independent of W^∘. With ordinary Hecke algebras 𝓗^{?,ord}_{G_*,U^p_*,A} := 𝓗^?_{G_*,U^p_*,A} ⊗_A A[T_{G_*}] ⊗_{Z_p[T^+_{G_*,0}]} Λ^∘_{G_*,U^p_*}, the module M^∘ ⊗ A is an 𝓗^{ord}-module with [t] acting by U_t.
items.locator: §3.1.2 (Ordinary completed homology) and §3.1.3, display (3.1.4), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Freeness, weight-independence and Hida control for G and H
items.statement: Proposition 3.1.2, parts 1–3 for G_* = G and H. M^∘_{G_*,U^p_*,W} is a projective Λ^∘_{G_*,U^p_*} ⊗ O_L-module of finite type; there are natural 𝓗^{ord}-equivariant isomorphisms j_W : M_{G_*,U^p_*} ⊗ O_L ≅ M_{G_*,U^p_*,W} induced by cap product with the highest-weight vector; and M_{G_*,U_*,W,r} := M ⊗_{Λ} Λ_{W,r} ≅ 𝓗_d(X̄_{*,r},𝓦)^{ord}.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1.2 with displays (3.1.5)–(3.1.7), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Hida, On p-adic Hecke algebras for GL_2 over totally real fields, §8; Hida, Control of nearly ordinary Hecke algebras, Theorem 1.2)
items.note: L5 plans exactly Hida control on the integral Hilbert automorphic/cohomology modules over the integral weight algebras, L0 the finite flatness of the ordinary Hecke algebras and L0a the ordinary projector. The abelian case G_* = H is the completed group algebra of a ray class group.

items.name: Ordinary completed homology of the product and of the quotient (G×H)'
items.statement: Proposition 3.1.2, part 1 for G×H and (G×H)'. By Künneth M^∘_{G×H,U^p×V^p} = M^∘_{G,U^p} ⊗̂ M^∘_{H,V^p}, a projective Λ^∘_{G×H} = Λ^∘_G ⊗̂ Λ^∘_H-module of finite type; and for K^p the image of U^p × V^p, M^∘_{(G×H)',K^p} = M^∘_{G×H,U^p×V^p}/(F^×_{A^∞}/F^× · ((U^p ∩ F^×_{A^{p∞}}) ∩ (V^p ∩ F^×_{A^{p∞}}))). This last is a quotient by a free action of a finite group, so M^∘_{(G×H)',K^p} is of finite type over Λ^∘_{(G×H)',K^p} and M_{(G×H)',K^p} is projective over Λ_{(G×H)'} after inverting p, the quotient map admitting a section there.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1.2 part 1 and display (3.1.8), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The ordinary Hecke algebra, the ordinary eigenvariety and its classical points
items.statement: T^{sph,ord}_{G_*,U^p_*,A} is the image of 𝓗^{?,ord}_{G_*,U^p_*,A} in End_A(M^∘_{G_*,U^p_*} ⊗ A), independent of the spherical Hecke algebra chosen; 𝓔^{ord}_{G_*,U_*^p} := Spec T^{sph,ord}_{G_*,U^p_*,Q_p} with κ_{G_*} : 𝓔^{ord} → 𝔚 and the ind-subschemes 𝓔^{ord,cl,(W)}_{(r)} := 𝔚^{cl,(W)}_{(r)} ×_{𝔚,κ} 𝓔^{ord} of classical points. 𝓜_{G_*,U^p_*} is the coherent sheaf attached to M_{G_*,U^p_*}. For G_* = (G×H)' the subscripts are omitted; (3.1.8) gives a closed immersion 𝓔^{ord}_{K^p} ↪ 𝓔^{ord}_{G×H,U^p×V^p}. A Hida family is an irreducible component X ⊂ 𝓔^{ord}_{K^p}, with X^{cl} := X ∩ 𝓔^{ord,cl}.
items.locator: §3.1.4 (Ordinary eigenvarieties) with displays (3.1.9)–(3.1.10) and §1.3.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The ordinary Hecke algebra is finite flat over the Iwasawa algebra
items.statement: Proposition 3.1.3. T^{sph,ord}_{G_*,U^p_*} is finite flat over Λ^∘_{G_*,U^p_*}, hence semi-local, and its maximal ideals are in bijection with G_{F_p}-orbits of characters λ̄ : T^{sph,ord}_{G_*,U^p_*} → F̄_p.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1.3, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)
items.note: L0 plans finite generation and finite flatness of the ordinary cuspidal Hecke algebras over the weight Iwasawa algebra with the exact level and residual-localization hypotheses; L5 the totally real instantiation.

items.name: Zariski-density of the classical points of a fixed weight
items.statement: Lemma 3.1.4. For an irreducible algebraic representation W of G_*, the set 𝓔^{ord,cl,W}_{G_*,U_*} of classical points of weight W is Zariski-dense in 𝓔^{ord}_{G_*,U^p_*}.
items.locator: Lemma 3.1.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (reduced, via finiteness of κ, to the density of 𝔚^{cl,W} in 𝔚)

items.name: The eigenvariety and universal character of the torus H
items.statement: M_{H,V^p} = Ĥ_0(Ȳ_{V^p}) = Z_p⟦Y_{V^p}(Ē)⟧ ⊗ Q_p, a principal homogeneous space for Γ_{E,V^p} = E^× \ E^×_{A^∞}/V^p, so 𝓔_{H,V^p} = Spec Z_p⟦Γ_{E,V^p}⟧_{Q_p}, whose classical points parametrise locally algebraic characters of Γ_{E,V^p}. 𝓜_{H,V^p} is a trivial line bundle and factors as χ^{−1}_{H,univ} ⊗ χ_univ, the Galois action being by the universal character χ_univ : G_E → Γ_{E,V^p} → Z_p⟦Γ_E⟧^× and the H(A^∞)-action by the inverse automorphic character.
items.locator: §3.1.5 (Abelian case), displays (3.1.11)–(3.1.12), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The fibres of 𝓜_G at classical points and the attached automorphic representation
items.statement: Proposition 3.1.5. For a classical x ∈ 𝓔^{ord,cl,W}_{G,U^p} of weight W and level r, with U = U^pU_{p,r}: (1) (𝓜_{G,U^p})_x ≅ 𝓗_1(X_{U,F̄},𝓦_{G,w̲})^{ord} ⊗_{𝓗^{sph},λ_x} Q_p(x) as 𝓗^{ord}-modules; (2) there is a unique automorphic representation π_x of G(A) over Q_p(x) with spherical character λ_x^p, weight W and unit character α_x^∘ = λ_{p}(U_·), and π_x^{ord,U^p} ≅ Hom_{Q_p(x)[G_{F,S}]}((𝓜_{G,U^p})_x, ρ_x).
items.locator: Proposition 3.1.5 with displays (3.1.13)–(3.1.14), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The fibre of 𝓜_{K^p} at a classical point and the vanishing of the central character
items.statement: Corollary 3.1.6. For z = (x,y) ∈ 𝓔^{ord,cl}_{K^p} and L = Q_p(z): ω_z := χ_{y|F^×_{A^{∞}}} ω_x = 1, and 𝓜_{K^p,z} ≅ ((π_x^{p,∨})^{U^p} ⊗_L χ_{H,y}^{−1,p}) ⊗_L (V_{x|G_{E,S}} ⊗_L χ_y) as 𝓗^{K_S}_{S,L} ⊗ L[G_{E,S}]-modules, the Galois group acting trivially on the first two factors.
items.locator: Corollary 3.1.6, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Étaleness of the weight map at classical points
items.statement: Proposition 3.1.7. κ : 𝓔^{ord}_{K^p} → 𝔚_{K^p} is étale over a neighbourhood of the classical points 𝔚^{cl}_{K^p}; in particular 𝓔^{ord}_{K^p} is regular at every z ∈ 𝓔^{ord,cl}_{K^p}.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1.7, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (via finite flatness and strong multiplicity one)

items.name: Isomorphic endomorphism Azumaya algebras come from a twist by a line bundle
items.statement: Lemma 3.2.1. Let X be an integral scheme and 𝓥_1, 𝓥_2 vector bundles of rank n > 0 with an isomorphism F : End_{O_X}(𝓥_1) → End_{O_X}(𝓥_2). Then there are an invertible O_X-module 𝓛 and an isomorphism g : 𝓥_1 ≅ 𝓥_2 ⊗ 𝓛 with F(T) ⊗ id_𝓛 = g T g^{−1} for every section T.
items.locator: Lemma 3.2.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (via Knus–Ojanguren: every automorphism of an Azumaya algebra is Zariski-locally inner)

items.name: Uniqueness of a representation with a given irreducible pseudocharacter
items.statement: Lemma 3.2.2. Let X be an integral scheme and 𝓣 : G_{F,S} → O(X) an irreducible pseudocharacter of dimension n, and let 𝓥_1, 𝓥_2 be representations of G_{F,S} with trace 𝓣. Then there are a line bundle 𝓛 with trivial Galois action and a G_{F,S}-equivariant isomorphism 𝓥_1 ≅ 𝓥_2 ⊗ 𝓛. (Input: 𝓐 := O_X[G]/Ker 𝓣 is Azumaya of rank 4 by Rouquier, and the natural maps 𝓐 → End(𝓥_i) are isomorphisms by Saltman; the irreducibility locus of a pseudocharacter is open.)
items.locator: Lemma 3.2.2 with §3.2.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Rouquier, Théorème 5.1; Saltman, Corollary 2.9; Chenevier §7.2.3)

items.name: The residual representation attached to a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra
items.statement: Lemma 3.2.3. For a character λ̄ : T^{sph,ord}_{G,U^p} → F̄_p there is a unique semisimple ρ̄ : G_{F,S} → GL_2(F̄_p) with Tr ρ̄(Fr_v) = q_v^{−1} λ̄(T_v) for all v ∉ S. Consequently 𝓔^{ord}_{G,U^p} decomposes as the disjoint union of the 𝓔^{ord}_{G,U^p,𝔪}, and a connected subset has a well-defined residual representation.
items.locator: Lemma 3.2.3 with display (3.2.3), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)
items.note: R19.6 plans the determinant law from Hecke operators and Frobenius polynomials together with its residual specialisations; L4 the decomposition of the ordinary Hecke algebra into residual components.

items.name: The rank-two Galois representation over a Hida family (Hida–Wiles)
items.statement: Proposition 3.2.4, except for the filtration in the residually reducible case. For an irreducible component X_G ⊂ 𝓔_G there are an open X'_G ⊃ X^{cl}_G and a locally free O_{X'_G}-module 𝓥_G of rank two with a G_{F,S}-action such that 𝓥_{G,x} ≅ V_{π_x} for all x ∈ X^{cl}_G; 𝓥_G is unique up to automorphisms and twists by line bundles with trivial Galois action.
items.locator: Proposition 3.2.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Hida and Wiles; see Fouquet §3.2.3)
items.note: L4 plans the ordinary big Galois representation on the Hecke component, first as a pseudorepresentation and then as a representation under the residual hypotheses, together with arithmetic specialization.

items.name: The ordinary filtration over a Hida family, including the residually reducible case
items.statement: Proposition 3.2.4, the filtration. Up to shrinking X'_G there is an exact sequence 0 → 𝓥^+_{G,v} → 𝓥_{G,v} → 𝓥^−_{G,v} → 0 of O_{X'_G}[G_{F_v}]-modules with 𝓥^±_{G,v} locally free of rank one and G_{F_v} acting on 𝓥^+_{G,v} by the character attached by local class field theory to α^∘_{|F_v^×}⟨·⟩_{F_v}. The proof is unconditional on the residual representation: with 𝓦^?_v := Hom(𝓥^+_{0,v},𝓥^?_{0,v}) one has H^0(F_v,𝓦^−_{v,x}) = H^2(F_v,𝓦^−_{v,x}) = 0, hence H^2(F_v,𝓦_{v,x}) = 0 and dim H^1(F_v,𝓦_{v,x}) = 1+2[F_v:Q_p] for all classical x; Proposition 5.2.3(3) then makes H^0(F_v,𝓦_v) a line bundle near X^{cl}_G, and 𝓥^+_{G,v} := H^0(F_v,𝓦_v) ⊗ 𝓥^+_{0,v}.
items.locator: Proposition 3.2.4 with displays (3.2.4)–(3.2.7) and the remark preceding its proof, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Schur's lemma over the Hida family
items.statement: Proposition 3.2.5. In the situation of Proposition 3.2.4 the natural injection O_{X'_G} → End_{O_{X'_G}[G_{F,S}]}(𝓥_G) is an isomorphism over an open X''_G ⊂ X_G containing X^{cl}.
items.locator: Proposition 3.2.5, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Constancy of the local level along a Hida family
items.statement: Lemma 3.3.1. For v ∉ Σ ∪ S_p the function x ↦ m_{x,v}, the v-level of π_{x,v} (the least m with π_{x,v}^{U_1(ϖ_v^m)} ≠ 0), is constant on X_G^{cl}; the common value is the v-level m_v of X_G, and one may assume U_v = U_1(ϖ_v^{m_v(X_G)}) (X_G is v-new).
items.locator: Lemma 3.3.1 with §3.3.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Carayol; Saha, Conductors in p-adic families, Theorem 3.4)

items.name: Descent of an irreducible component to its new level
items.statement: Lemma 3.3.2. Let 'X_G ⊂ 𝓔^{ord}_{G,U^{p}{}'} be an irreducible component with U^{p}{}' = ∏ U'_v; let U^p = ∏ U_v with U_v = U_1(ϖ_v^{m_v}) ⊇ U'_v for v ∉ Σ ∪ S_p and U_v = U'_v otherwise. Then there is a unique irreducible component X_G ⊂ 𝓔^{ord}_{G,U^p} whose image under 𝓔^{ord}_{G,U^p} ⊂ 𝓔^{ord}_{G,U^{p}{}'} is 'X_G.
items.locator: Lemma 3.3.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: A uniform level at the ramification set Σ along a Hida family
items.statement: Lemma 3.3.3. For v ∈ Σ there is a compact open U'_v ⊂ U_v such that π_{x',v}^{U'_v} = π_{x',v} for every classical x' ∈ X_G. (Proof: the Galois family 𝓥_G gives a map f : X_G → 𝔛_v to the Bernstein variety of GL_2(F_v) compatible with local Langlands; on each connected component the inertial class is either supercuspidal, in which case the fibres differ by an unramified twist, or Steinberg-type, in which case the classical points land in the closed Steinberg stratum, the remaining case being excluded because only special and supercuspidal representations lie in the image of Jacquet–Langlands.)
items.locator: Lemma 3.3.3, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Disegni, Local Langlands correspondence…in analytic families, Theorem 3.2.1)

items.name: The H'_Σ-invariants are a direct summand
items.statement: Lemma 3.3.4. 𝓥 := 𝓜^{H'_Σ}_{K_0^{p}{}'} is a direct summand of 𝓜_{K_0^{p}{}'}: the compact group H'_Σ = ∏_{v ∈ Σ} E_v^×/F_v^× acts on the locally free sheaf through a finite quotient, so the inclusion splits.
items.locator: Lemma 3.3.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The geometric incarnation 𝓥 of the universal Galois representation
items.statement: Proposition 3.3.5. There is an open X^{(1)} ⊂ X containing all classical points over which 𝓥 = 𝓜^{H'_Σ}_{K_0^{p}{}'} is locally free of rank 2, and for z = (x,y) ∈ X^{cl}, 𝓥_z ≅ V_x ⊗ χ_y as a G_{F,E,S}-representation. (The two extra factors in 𝓥_z ≅ (π_x^{∨,Σp,U_0^{Σp}} ⊗ χ_y^{−1,Σp}) ⊗ (π^∨_{x,Σ} ⊗ χ^{−1}_{y,Σ})^{H'_Σ} ⊗ (V_x ⊗ χ_y) are one-dimensional, the first by the theory of local newforms and the second by the local distinction hypothesis (ε_v)'.)
items.locator: Proposition 3.3.5 with display (3.3.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Comparison of the geometric and the abstract universal representation
items.statement: Corollary 3.3.6. There are an open X^{(2)} ⊂ X^{(0)} ∩ X^{(1)} containing X^{cl} with End_{O_{X^{(2)}}[G_{F,E,S}]}(𝓥) = O_{X^{(2)}}, an invertible sheaf 𝓛 with trivial Galois action, and a G_{F,E,S}-equivariant isomorphism 𝓥 ≅ 𝓛 ⊗ 𝓥', where 𝓥' = (𝓥_G ⊠ χ_univ)_{|X^{(0)}}.
items.locator: Corollary 3.3.6 with §3.3.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Openness of the locus where a square map of free modules specialises to an isomorphism
items.statement: Lemma 3.3.7. For a ring R and a map T : M → N of free R-modules of the same rank, the set of x ∈ Spec R at which T ⊗ R/𝔭_x is an isomorphism is open, being the complement of V(det T).
items.locator: Lemma 3.3.7, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)
items.note: The locus is the basic open set D(det T) of Spec R and a square matrix over a commutative ring is invertible exactly when its determinant is; both facts are in Mathlib at the pinned commit.

items.name: Cofinal levels, the universal representation and the factorisation of 𝓜
items.statement: Proposition 3.3.8. Fix a finite Σ' disjoint from Σ ∪ S_p and let 𝓤 be the set of U^{p}{}' = ∏ U'_v ⊂ U^p with U'_v as in Lemma 3.3.3 for v ∈ Σ and U'_v = U_v for v ∉ Σ' ∪ Σ ∪ S_p. Then: (1) there are a cofinal sequence (U^p_i{}') ⊂ 𝓤, opens X_i ⊂ X^{(2)} containing X^{cl}, integers r_i and G_{F,E}-equivariant maps T_i : 𝓥^{⊕r_i} → 𝓜^{H'_Σ}_{K^p_i{}'} that are isomorphisms over X_i, built from Casselman's oldform degeneracy operators; (2) for each U^{p}{}' ∈ 𝓤 there is an open X_{U^{p}{}'} ⊃ X^{cl} over which Π^{K^{p}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ} := Hom_{O_X[G_{F,E,S}]}(𝓜^{H'_Σ}_{K^{p}{}'},𝓥) is locally free and 𝓜^{H'_Σ}_{K^{p}{}'} ≅ (Π^{K^{p}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ})^∨ ⊗ 𝓥, with Π^{K^{p}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ} ⊂ Π^{K^{p}{}'',ord}_{H'_Σ} for U^{p}{}'' ⊂ U^{p}{}'; (3) Π^{K^{p}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ} is generated over 𝓗_{G×H,Σ'}^{K^{p}{}'} by Π^{K_0^{p}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ}; (4) for z = (x,y) ∈ X^{cl}, (Π^{K^{p}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ})_z ≅ (π_x^{U^{p}{}',ord})_{H'_Σ} ⊗ χ_y.
items.locator: Proposition 3.3.8 with displays (3.3.2)–(3.3.3), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Casselman, On some results of Atkin and Lehner)

items.name: The universal ordinary representation
items.statement: Definition 3.3.9. With X^{(3)} := X_{U^{p}{}'} and Π^{K^{p}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ} as above, the universal ordinary representation Π^{K^{Sp},ord}_{H'_Σ} is the O_{X^{(3)}}[(B^×_{Σ'} × E^×_{Σ'})/F^×_{Σ'}]-submodule of 'Π^{K^{Sp},ord}_{H'_Σ} := colim_{U^{p}{}'' ∈ 𝓤} Π^{K^{p}{}'',ord} generated by Π^{K^{p}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ}.
items.locator: Definition 3.3.9 with §3.3.3, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence in analytic families for GL_2
items.statement: To a family 𝓥_G of representations of ∏_{v ∈ Σ'} G_{F_v} on a rank-two locally free sheaf over a Noetherian Q-scheme Y, the correspondence of [LLC] attaches a family π_{G,Σ'}(𝓥_G) of representations of GL_2(F_{Σ'}) on a torsion-free sheaf over Y, co-Whittaker in the sense of [LLC, Definition 4.2.2] and so with a unique Whittaker model; it is compatible with the Bernstein-variety map of supercuspidal supports, and if a smooth finitely generated admissible module has the right fibres at a dense set of points then it agrees with π_{G,Σ'}(𝓥_G) up to a line bundle over an open subset ([LLC, Theorem 4.4.3]). The normalisation of [LLC] differs from Theorem 2.5.1(1) by a Tate twist.
items.locator: §3.3.4 and Theorem 3.3.10 (used as an input), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024); Disegni, Local Langlands correspondence, local factors, and zeta integrals in analytic families, J. Lond. Math. Soc. (2) 101 (2020), 735–764, Theorems 3.2.1 and 4.4.3

items.name: Local–global compatibility for the universal ordinary representation
items.statement: Theorem 3.3.10. There are an open X^{(4)} ⊂ X^{(3)} containing X^{cl}, a line bundle Π^{K^{Sp}{}',S,ord}_{H'_Σ} over X^{(4)} and an isomorphism of O_{X^{(4)}}[GL_2(F_{Σ'}) × E^×_{Σ'}]-modules Π^{K^{Sp}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ} ≅ (π_{G,Σ'}(𝓥_G) ⊗_{O_{X^{(3)}}} χ_{H,univ,Σ'}) ⊗ Π^{K^{Sp}{}',S,ord}_{H'_Σ}.
items.locator: Theorem 3.3.10 with display (3.3.4), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: ε-symmetric and ε-hermitian pairings
items.statement: For ε ∈ {±1}, a ring or sheaf of rings R and R-modules M, J, an R-bilinear (,) : M ⊗ M → J is ε-symmetric if (m,m') = ε(m',m). If R carries an involution ι, writing (·)^ι for ⊗_{R,ι}R and m ↦ m ⊗ 1, an (R,ι)-sesquilinear (,) : M ⊗ M^ι → J is ε-hermitian if (m,n) = ε·ι((n^ι,m^ι)^ι). The prefix 'skew-' means ε = −1.
items.locator: §4.1.1 (Pairings, symmetries and involutions), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The involution ι and duality of ordinary parts
items.statement: Lemma 4.1.1. For an irreducible algebraic W of G_* over L: (1) σ_{W^∨}(t) = σ_W(t^ι) for all t ∈ T_{G_*}; (2) if π^{ord} is the ordinary part of an automorphic representation of G_*(A^∞) over L of weight W, unramified of level U^S_*, there is an isomorphism of 𝓗^{sph,ord}_{G_*,U^S}-modules π^{∨,U^S_*,ord} ≅ (π^{U^S_*,ord})^ι; (3) there is an identification (𝓔^{cl,W}_{G_*})^ι = 𝓔^{cl,W^∨}_{G_*} with π^{ord}_{ι(x)} = (π_x)^{∨,ord}. In the proof of (2) the displayed relation for the local components must be read as an embedding π_v^∨ ↪ Ind(α_v^ι·(|·|_v,|·|_v^{−1})), not an isomorphism (Correction, Errata).
items.locator: Lemma 4.1.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024); the corrected symbol in the third-last line of its proof is recorded in Appendix B, Errata

items.name: The pairing on Hom-spaces induced by a duality of homology
items.statement: Construction 4.1.2. Let A be a ring, G a group and M_1, M_2, V_1, V_2, A(d) be A[G]-modules, projective of finite type over A; write V^D := Hom(V,A(d)). Given f_i ∈ π_i := Hom(M_i,V_i), an identification V_2^D ≅ V_1 and a perfect pairing ⟨,⟩ : M_1 × M_2 → A(d) with induced u_{⟨,⟩} : M_2^D → M_1, one sets (f_1,f_2)_{⟨,⟩} := f_1 ∘ u_{⟨,⟩}(f_2^D) ∈ End_{A[G]}(V_1).
items.locator: Construction 4.1.2 with display (4.1.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Poincaré duality pairings on the homology of the Shimura tower
items.statement: Fixing lattices W^∘, W^{∨,∘} and the invariant pairing ⟨,⟩^W : W ⊗ W^∨ → L, integral up to a bounded denominator p^{−|W|}, one has ⟨,⟩_{U_*,W} : H_d(X̄_{*,U_*},𝓦) × H_d(X̄_{*,U_*},𝓦^∨) → H_0(X̄_{*,U_*},𝓦⊗𝓦^∨) → L(d), satisfying ⟨xT,y⟩ = ⟨x,yT^ι⟩ for T ∈ 𝓗^p_{G_*,U_*} and the projection formula ⟨p_{U'/U,*}x,y⟩_{W,U} = ⟨x,p^*_{U'/U}y⟩_{W,U'}.
items.locator: §4.1.3 and §4.1.4 (Homological dualities /1), displays (4.1.2)–(4.1.3), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Trace and group-algebra promotions of a bilinear form
items.statement: Lemma 4.1.3. Let R be a ring, S a finite R-algebra, M a finite S-module. (1) If S/R is étale there is a natural isomorphism α : Hom_R(M,R) → Hom_S(M,S), λ ↦ (m ↦ (s ↦ λ(sm))) composed with S ≅ Hom_R(S,R) given by the trace. (2) If S = R[T] for a finite abelian group T there is an isomorphism β : Hom_R(M,R) → Hom_{R[T]}(M,R[T]), λ ↦ (m ↦ Σ_t λ(tm)[t^{−1}]). If S = R[T] is étale over R then α(λ) = |T|^{−1}β(λ). Explicitly ⟨,⟩ ↦ ⟨⟨x,y⟩⟩ := Σ_{t ∈ T} ⟨x,ty⟩[t^{−1}].
items.locator: Lemma 4.1.3 with §4.1.5, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The Λ_H-valued pairing on the completed homology of the torus
items.statement: Applying Lemma 4.1.3(2) with M = M_{H,V^p,r,W} ⊗ M_{H,V^p,r,W^∨}, R = L and S = Λ_{H,V^p,r} ≅ L[T̄_{H,0}/T̄_{H,r}], the Poincaré pairings give ⟨⟨,⟩⟩_{V^p,W,r} and, in the limit, a well-defined ⟨⟨,⟩⟩_{V^p,W} : M_{H,V^p,W} ⊗_{Λ_H} M^ι_{H,V^p,W^∨} → Λ_H ⊗ L = O_{𝓔_H} ⊗ L.
items.locator: §4.1.5, display (4.1.4), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The normalised automorphic inner product and its ordinary modification
items.statement: With v(U_*) = vol(X_{*,U_*}(C)) for the hyperbolic metric dxdy/2πy² (resp. the counting metric for H), so that deg p_{U'_*,U_*} = v(U'_*)/v(U_*) and v(U^p_*) := v(U^p_*U_{*,0}(p^r)_p)/p^{dr[F:Q]}, Construction 4.1.2 applied to the Poincaré pairings gives (,)_{π,U_*} : π^{U_*} × π^{∨,U_*} → L, and the limit (,)_π := lim_{U_*} (dim W · v(U_*))^{−1}(,)_{π,U_*} : π × π^∨ → L is well defined. For an ordinary π one sets (f_1,f_2)^{ord}_π := dim W · (w_a^{ord}f_1, f_2)_π on π^{ord} × π^{∨,ord}.
items.locator: §4.1.6 (Automorphic inner products), displays (4.1.5)–(4.1.8), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The twisted Poincaré pairing on ordinary homology
items.locator: §4.1.7 (Homological dualities /3), display (4.1.9), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Comparison of the ordinary automorphic pairing with the twisted Poincaré pairing
items.statement: Lemma 4.1.4. For an ordinary π, identifying π^{ord} = Hom_{L[G_{E_*}]}(𝓗_1(X̄_{*,U^p_*,r},𝓦)^{ord},V_π) for large r, the pairing produced by Construction 4.1.2 from ⟨,⟩^{ord}_{U_*,W,r} satisfies (,)^{ord}_π = v(U_*)^{−1}(,)_{⟨,⟩^{ord}_{U_*,W,r}}.
items.locator: Lemma 4.1.4, display (4.1.10), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Hecke equivariance and the Λ-valued Poincaré pairing in the ordinary tower
items.statement: Lemma 4.1.5. The pairings ⟨⟨,⟩⟩_{W,r} satisfy ⟨⟨x_rT,y_r⟩⟩ = ⟨⟨x_r,y_rT^ι⟩⟩ for T ∈ 𝓗^{ord}_{G,r}, and the limit ⟨⟨,⟩⟩_{Λ,U^p_*,W} : M_{G_*,U^p_*,𝓦} ⊗_{𝓗^{ord}_G} M^ι_{G_*,U^p_*,𝓦^∨} → Λ_{G_*,U^p_*}(d) ⊗ L is well defined.
items.locator: Lemma 4.1.5 with display (4.1.11), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Independence of the Λ-valued pairing from the weight
items.statement: Lemma 4.1.6. The square relating ⟨⟨,⟩⟩_{Λ,U^p_*,W} on M_{G_*,U^p_*,𝓦} ⊗ M^ι_{G_*,U^p_*,𝓦^∨} and ⟨⟨,⟩⟩_{Λ,U^p_*} on M_{G_*,U^p_*} ⊗ M^ι_{G_*,U^p_*}, whose left vertical map is j_W ⊗ j_{W^∨} from Proposition 3.1.2(2) and whose right vertical map is [t] ↦ σ_W^{−1}(t)[t], commutes.
items.locator: Lemma 4.1.6, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Skew-hermitian dualities over the Hida family
items.statement: Proposition 4.1.7. Let X^{(5)} ⊃ X^{cl} be the intersection of X^{(4)} with the locus where X → Spec Λ_{Q_p} is étale. There exist: a perfect, G_E-equivariant, skew-hermitian pairing 𝓜^{H'_Σ}_{K^{p}{}'} ⊗_{O_{X^{(5)}}} 𝓜^{H'_Σ,ι}_{K^{p}{}'} → O_{X^{(5)}}(1); a perfect, G_E-equivariant, skew-hermitian pairing 𝓥 ⊗ 𝓥^ι → O_{X^{(5)}}(1); and a perfect pairing ((,)) := v(K^{p}{}')^{−1}(,)_{⟨⟨,⟩⟩_{K^{p}{}'}} : Π^{K^{p}{}'}_{H'_Σ} ⊗_{O_{X^{(5)}}} (Π^{K^{p}{}'}_{H'_Σ})^ι → O_{X^{(5)}}, deduced from the first two through Construction 4.1.2 and Proposition 3.3.8(2).
items.locator: Proposition 4.1.7 with displays (4.1.12)–(4.1.14), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Specialisation of the family pairing to the ordinary automorphic pairing
items.statement: Proposition 4.1.8. For global sections f_1 of Π^{K^{p}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ} and f_2 of its ι-twist: (1) if f_{i,W,r} are the specialisations of f_i then ((f_1,f_2))|_{X^{cl,W}_r} = ((f_{1,W,r},f_{2,W,r}))_{W,r}; (2) if the maps f_{i,x} factor through the projections to 𝓗_1(Z̄_{K^{p}{}',r},𝓦^?)^{ord}_{H'_Σ} = M^{H'_Σ}_{K^{p}{}',W,r} and coincide with the specialisations of f_{i,W,r}, then ((f_1,f_2))_{W,r}(x) = (f_{1,x},f_{2,x})^{ord}_π = dim W · (w_a^{ord}f_1,f_2)_π.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1.8 with display (4.1.15), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The normalising local L-value 𝓛(V_{(π,χ),v},0)
items.statement: For a place v of F, 𝓛(V_{(π,χ),v},0) := ζ_{F,v}(2) L(V_v,0)/(L(1,η_v) L(ad(V_{π,v}),1)) times 1 if v is finite and π^{−[F:Q]} if v = ∞, where V_v is the restriction to G_{E_v} of the Galois representation attached to Π (the Hodge structure of W if v = ∞), η is the quadratic character of E/F, and the virtual motive is written V_{(π,χ),v} := (V_{π,v} ⊗ Ind_{F_v}^{E_v}χ_v) ⊖ ad(V_π)(1).
items.locator: §1.2.6 (Local toric periods), display (1.2.5), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The normalised local and global toric pairings Q
items.statement: For finite v, Q_{v,(,)_v,dt_v}(f_{1,v},f_{2,v}) := 𝓛(V_{(π,χ),v},0)^{−1} ∫_{H'_v} (Π_v(t)f_{1,v},f_{2,v})_v dt_v, an absolutely convergent integral and an explicit generator of Π_v^{*,H'_v} ⊗ (Π_v^∨)^{*,H'_v}; for v = ∞, ∫_{H'_∞}Π_∞(t)dt_∞ := vol(H'_∞,dt_∞)·p_{H'_∞} : W → W_{H'_∞} = W^{H'_∞}. The quotient Q_{v,dt_v}(f_{1,v}⊗f_{2,v}/f_{3,v}⊗f_{4,v}) := Q_{v,(,)_v,dt_v}(f_{1,v},f_{2,v})/(f_{3,v},f_{4,v})_v is independent of (,)_v and equals vol(O_{E,v}^×/O_{F,v}^×,dt_v) when everything is unramified. Fixing measures with vol(H'(Q)\H'(A),dt) = 1, Q(f_1⊗f_2/f_3⊗f_4) := ∏_v Q_{v,dt_v}(f_{1,v}⊗f_{2,v}/f_{3,v}⊗f_{4,v}).
items.locator: §1.2.6, displays (1.2.6)–(1.2.8), and §4.2 with displays (4.2.1)–(4.2.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)
items.note: GZ.4 plans exactly the normalized toric matrix-coefficient integrals with their convergence or regularization, rationality under coefficient embeddings, invariance under rescaling of the local pairings and measures, and the unramified value making the product finite.

items.name: Tunnell–Saito multiplicity one and the epsilon dichotomy
items.statement: The space Π^{*,H'(A)} = Hom_{H'(A)}(Π,L) is nonzero if and only if, for every v, ε^G_v(V) := ε(V_v)χ_v(−1)η_v(−1)ε(B_v) = +1, where ε(B_v) = +1 or −1 according as B_v is split or not; in that case it is one-dimensional and the global root number is ε(V) = −1. Conversely, for V with ε(V) = −1 there is a unique incoherent totally definite B satisfying all the (ε_v). The condition (ε_∞) is equivalent to (wt).
items.locator: §1.2.5 (Multiplicity one), display (1.2.4), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Waldspurger; Tunnell; H. Saito)
items.note: GZ.4 plans Saito–Tunnell multiplicity one and the epsilon dichotomy for a quadratic étale algebra in a quaternion algebra, split and nonsplit tori treated separately, with the archimedean discrete-series contribution.

items.name: Locally distinguished representations and Hida families
items.statement: Definition 1.2.1: Π is locally distinguished by H' if it satisfies (ε_v) for all v. Definition 1.3.1: a Hida family X for (G×H)' is locally distinguished if for every (equivalently one) classical point z of weight satisfying (wt) the Galois representation 𝓥_z attached to Π_z satisfies (ε_v), for all v ∤ p∞.
items.locator: Definitions 1.2.1 and 1.3.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The toric pairing as a product of zeta integrals in the split case
items.statement: When E = F ⊕ F, so that G = GL_2(F), Kirillov models with the pairing (f,f^∨) = ζ(2)L(1,π×π^∨)^{−1}∫_{F^×}f(y)f^∨(y)d^×y identify Q_{(,)_,dt}(f ⊗ e_χ, f^∨ ⊗ e_{χ^{−1}}) up to constants in L^× with the product (L(1/2,π⊗χ_1)^{−1}I(f,χ_1,1/2))·(L(1/2,π⊗χ_1)^{−1}I(f^∨,χ_1,1/2)) of two GL_2 × GL_1 zeta integrals, where χ = (χ_1,χ_2), χ_2 = ω^{−1}χ_1.
items.locator: §4.2.1, display (4.2.4), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The unramified value of the toric pairing (Waldspurger)
items.statement: Lemma 4.2.1. If B is split, E/F unramified and π, χ unramified, then for a maximal compact K ⊂ (G × E^×)/F^× and v ∈ Π^K, w ∈ (Π^∨)^K one has Q_{(,),dt}(v,w) = vol(O_E^×/O_F^×,dt)·(v,w).
items.locator: Lemma 4.2.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Waldspurger, Compositio Math. 54 (1985), Lemme 14)
items.note: GZ.4 plans the unramified value of the normalized toric integral, which is exactly this computation.

items.name: The toric pairing on the line of H'-invariants when B is nonsplit
items.statement: Lemma 4.2.2. If B is nonsplit, so that Π is finite-dimensional and H' compact, then on the line Π^{H'} ⊗ Π^{∨,H'} one has Q_{(,),dt} = 𝓛(V_{(π,χ),v},0)^{−1} vol(E^×/F^×,dt)·(,).
items.locator: Lemma 4.2.2 with §4.2.3, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The ordinary toric pairing Q^{ord}
items.statement: Definition 4.3.1. With μ^+_v the character by which E_v^× acts on V^+_{π,v} ⊗ χ_v, j_v the fixed purely imaginary element, μ^+(j) := ∏_{v|p}μ^+_v(j_v), and the normalised volumes vol^∘(H'_v,dt_v) := vol(O^×_{E,v}/O^×_{F,v},dt_v)/(e_v L(1,η_v)^{−1}), vol^∘(H'_{v,∞},dt_{v,∞}) := vol(H'_{v,∞},dt_{v,∞})/2^{[F_v:Q_p]}, one sets Q^{ord}_{dt_{p∞}}(f_{1,p∞}⊗f_{2,p∞}/f_{3,p∞}⊗f_{4,p∞}) := μ^+(j)·vol^∘(H'_{p∞},dt_{p∞})·(f_{1,p∞}⊗f_{2,p∞})/(f_{3,p∞}⊗f_{4,p∞}), and Q^{ord} := Q^{p∞}_{dt^{p∞}} · Q^{ord}_{dt_{p∞}}.
items.locator: Definition 4.3.1 with displays (4.3.1)–(4.3.3), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Nonvanishing of the ordinary toric functional
items.statement: Remark 4.3.2. If Π is locally distinguished, so that Q_{dt} is nonzero, then Q^{ord}_{dt} is also nonzero.
items.locator: Remark 4.3.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Decomposition of Q^{ord} into local factors
items.statement: Lemma 4.3.3. For f_1,f_3 ∈ Π^{K^p,ord}_{H'_Σ}, f_2,f_4 ∈ Π^{∨,K^p,ord}_{H'_Σ} with (f_3,f_4)^{ord} ≠ 0, Q^{ord}(f_1⊗f_2/f_3⊗f_4) equals ∏_{v ∈ Σ'}Q_{v,dt_v}(·) times ∏_{v ∈ Σ} vol(E_v^×/F_v^×,dt)𝓛(V_{(π,χ),v},0)^{−1}(f_{1,v}⊗f_{2,v})/(f_{3,v}⊗f_{4,v}) times the away-from-Sp∞ ratio times Q^{ord}_{p∞,dt_{p∞}}(·).
items.locator: Lemma 4.3.3, display (4.3.4), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Comparison of the toric pairing with its ordinary variant
items.statement: Proposition 4.3.4. For an ordinary Π = π ⊗ χ = Π^∞ ⊗ W of (G×H)'(A), with w_a^{ord} and γ^{ord}_{H'} the operators of Propositions A.2.1 and A.2.4 and e_p(V_{(π,χ)}) the p-part of the interpolation factor, one has Q(γ^{ord}_{H'}(f_1) ⊗ γ^{ord}_{H'}(f_2) / w_a^{ord}(f_3) ⊗ f_4) = e_p(V_{(π,χ)})·dim W·Q^{ord}(f_1⊗f_2/f_3⊗f_4).
items.locator: Proposition 4.3.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Interpolation of the local L-factors of a family of Weil–Deligne representations
items.statement: Lemma 4.4.1. Let X be a Q-scheme and r' = (r,N) a Weil–Deligne representation of W_F on a rank-two locally free sheaf, with a dense X^{cl} at whose points r'_x is pure. Then there are an open X'' ⊃ X^{cl} and functions L(0,r')^{−1}, L(1,r',ad) ∈ O(X'') specialising at every point of X'' to L(0,r'_x)^{−1} and L(1,ad(r'_x)).
items.locator: Lemma 4.4.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Interpolation of the local toric pairings
items.statement: Proposition 4.4.2. In the situation of Lemma 4.4.1, let π = π(r') be the module attached to r' by the local Langlands correspondence in families, ω its central character and χ : E^× → O(X)^× with ωχ|_{F^×} = 1, Π = π ⊗ χ, Π^∨ = π(ρ^*(1)) ⊗ χ^{−1}. Then there are an open X' ⊃ X^{cl}, an O^×-submodule (Π ⊗_{O^×}Π^∨)^× specialising to the locus where (f_3,f_4) ≠ 0, and a map of O-modules 𝓠_{dt} : (Π ⊗_O Π^∨) ⊗_{O^×}(Π ⊗_{O^×}Π^∨)^{×,−1} → 𝓚 which is E^×/F^×-equivariant in the first two variables and denominator-invariant in the last two, and whose specialisation at every x ∈ X^{cl} is Q_{dt}.
items.locator: Proposition 4.4.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The interpolated global toric functional 𝓠 over the Hida family
items.statement: Theorem 4.4.3. With Π := Π^{K^{p}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ} over X^{(5)} and the submodule (Π ⊗_{𝓚}Π^ι)^× defined by (f_3,f_4) ≠ 0 and (f_{3,v},f_{4,v})_v ≠ 0 for v ∈ Σ', there are an open X^{(6)} ⊂ X^{(5)} containing X^{cl} and a map of O^×-modules 𝓠 : (Π ⊗_O Π^ι) ⊗_{O^×}(Π ⊗_{O^×}Π^ι)^{×,−1} → 𝓚_X such that 𝓠(Π_{Σ'}(t_1)f_1 ⊗ Π^ι_{Σ'}(t_2)f_2 / Π(h)f_3 ⊗ f_4) = 𝓠(f_1⊗f_2 / f_3 ⊗ Π^ι(h)f_4) for t_i ∈ E^×_{Σ'}/F^×_{Σ'} and h ∈ 𝓗_{S,K_{Σ'}}, and 𝓠_{|x} = Q^{ord} for every x ∈ X^{cl}.
items.locator: Theorem 4.4.3 with display (4.4.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Admissible and ind-admissible modules and their continuous cochains
items.statement: For a complete Noetherian local ring (R^∘,𝔪) and a topological group G, an R^∘[G]-module M is admissible of finite type if it is of finite type over R^∘ and the action G × M → M is continuous for the 𝔪-adic topology, and ind-admissible if it is the union of its finite-type admissible submodules. C^•_cont(G,M) is defined in the usual way in the first case and as the colimit in the second; RΓ(G,M) is its image in D(_R Mod), with cohomology H^i(G,M). For R = R^∘[𝓢^{−1}] and M = M^∘ ⊗_{R^∘} R one has C^•_cont(G,M) ≅ C^•_cont(G,M^∘) ⊗_{R^∘} R.
items.locator: §5.1.1–§5.1.2, display (5.1.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Nekovář, Selmer complexes, (3.4.1), (3.7.4))

items.name: Continuous cohomology of ind-admissible sheaves on the category 𝓒_{R^∘}
items.statement: Remark 5.1.1. Let 𝓒 = 𝓒_{R^∘} be the category of schemes isomorphic to open subschemes of Spec R^∘ with open immersions as maps. For any object X of 𝓒 the condition of ind-admissibility is defined for all quasi-coherent O_X[G]-modules, the functors RΓ(G,−) are defined on them, and both are compatible with restriction along open immersions. For complete Noetherian local R^∘_1, R^∘_2 with R^∘ = R^∘_1 ⊗̂ R^∘_2 there is a functor ⊗̂ : 𝓒_{R^∘_1} × 𝓒_{R^∘_2} → 𝓒_{R^∘} given on objects by Spec R^∘_1[1/f_1] ⊗̂ Spec R^∘_2[1/f_2] := Spec (R^∘_1⊗̂R^∘_2)[1/f_1⊗1,1/1⊗f_2] and glueing.
items.locator: Remark 5.1.1 and §5.1.3 with display (5.1.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: RΓ(G,−) as an exact functor on ind-admissible complexes
items.statement: Proposition 5.1.2. RΓ(G,−) extends to bounded-below complexes of ind-admissible O_X[G]-modules with values in bounded-below complexes of O_X-modules and descends to an exact functor D^+(_{O_X[G]}^{ind-adm}Mod) → D^+(_{O_X}Mod). For i = 0,1 the functors M ↦ H^i(G,M) on ind-admissible R-modules are the derived functors of M ↦ M^G.
items.locator: Proposition 5.1.2 and §5.1.5, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Nekovář, Selmer complexes, (3.5.6), (3.6.2)(v))

items.name: Base change for continuous cohomology
items.statement: Proposition 5.1.3. Let M be an ind-admissible O_X[G]-module and N an O_X-module of finite projective dimension. Then there is a natural isomorphism RΓ(G,M) ⊗^L_{O_X} N ≅ RΓ(G, M ⊗^L_{O_X} N) in D^b(_{O_X}Mod). This applies when N = O_Y for a local complete intersection Y ⊂ X, or when X is regular and N is coherent. If R ↠ R' = R/I then C^•_cont(G,M') is the same computed over R or R'; more generally the functor on O_Y[G]-modules for a closed Y ⊂ X is the restriction of the one on O_X[G]-modules.
items.locator: Proposition 5.1.3 with §5.1.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Base change at a nonsingular point and the specialisation spectral sequence
items.statement: Corollary 5.1.4. For an ind-admissible O_X[G]-module M flat over O_X and a nonsingular x ∈ X there is an isomorphism RΓ(G,M) ⊗^L_{O_X} κ(x) ≅ RΓ(G, M ⊗_{O_X} κ(x)) in D^b(_{κ(x)}Mod), hence a second-quadrant spectral sequence Tor_{−p}(H^q(G,M),κ(x)) ⇒ H^{q−p}(G, M ⊗_{O_X}κ(x)).
items.locator: Corollary 5.1.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The finiteness condition (F) and the p-cohomological dimension
items.statement: A profinite group G satisfies (F) if H^i(G,M) is finite for every finite discrete F_p[G]-module and every i ≥ 0; cd_p(G) := sup{i : H^i(G,M) ≠ 0 for some finite discrete F_p[G]-module M}. For a number field E and a finite set S of places, G_{E,S} satisfies (F) with cd_p = 3; for a local field E_w, G_{E_w} satisfies (F) with cd_p = 2.
items.locator: §5.2.1 (Finiteness conditions), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)
items.note: R02.3 plans global finiteness and cohomology with restricted ramification, including the finiteness of H^i(G_{E,S},M) for finite modules and the cohomological dimension; L0 imports it.

items.name: Finiteness and vanishing of the cohomology of ind-admissible sheaves
items.statement: Lemma 5.2.1. If G satisfies (F) then the cohomology groups of ind-admissible O_X[G]-modules of finite type are O_X-modules of finite type, and the cohomology of any ind-admissible O_X[G]-module vanishes in degrees above cd_p(G).
items.locator: Lemma 5.2.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Nekovář, Selmer complexes, (4.2.5), (4.2.10), (4.2.6))

items.name: Cohomology commutes with countable projective limits of admissible modules
items.statement: Lemma 5.2.2. Let G be a profinite group satisfying (F) and M = lim_n M_n the limit of a countable projective system of admissible R^∘-modules of finite type. Then H^i(G,M) → lim_n H^i(G,M_n) is an isomorphism for all i.
items.locator: Lemma 5.2.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Support of higher cohomology and specialisation of H^{i_0} and H^0
items.statement: Proposition 5.2.3. Let G satisfy (F) with cd_p(G) = e < ∞, M an ind-admissible O_X[G]-module of finite type, x ∈ X nonsingular, i_0 ≥ 0 with H^i(G, M ⊗_R κ(x)) = 0 for all i ≥ i_0+1. Then (1) for i ≥ i_0+1 the support of H^i(G,M) is a proper closed subset not containing x; (2) H^{i_0}(G,M) ⊗_{O_X} κ(x) → H^{i_0}(G, M ⊗_R κ(x)) is an isomorphism; (3) if moreover i_0 = 1 and dim_{κ(y)} H^1(G, M ⊗ κ(y)) is constant on a dense open subset and equals its value at x, then H^0(G,M) ⊗_R κ(x) → H^0(G, M ⊗_{O_X} κ(x)) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Proposition 5.2.3, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Greenberg data and the strict condition away from p
items.statement: Definition 5.3.1. A Greenberg datum (M,(M^+_w)_{w ∈ Sp}) over X consists of an ind-admissible O_X[G_{E,Sp}]-module M, finite and locally free over O_X, together with, for each w ∈ Sp, a short exact sequence 0 → M^+_w → M_w → M^−_w → 0 of ind-admissible O_X[G_w]-modules, finite and locally free over O_X. At w ∤ p only the strict condition M^+_w = 0 is used.
items.locator: Definition 5.3.1 with §5.3.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)
items.note: L2 plans local conditions defined as submodules or maps of complexes, with the unramified, strict, relaxed and Greenberg conditions defined separately and the filtration stable under a decomposition group at p. What L2 does not plan is the version over a base scheme X with ind-admissible sheaves, which is the separate item selmer-complex-over-X.

items.name: The Selmer complex of a Greenberg datum over a base, and its exact sequences
items.statement: For a Greenberg datum over X the Selmer complex R̃Γ_f(E,M) is the image in D(^{ft}_{O_X}Mod) of Cone(C^•_cont(G_{E,Sp},M) ⊕ ⊕_w C^•_cont(E_w,M^+_w) → ⊕_w C^•_cont(E_w,M_w))[−1] for the map ⊕_w res_w − i^+_{w,*}; its cohomology is H̃^i_f(E,M). There is an exact triangle R̃Γ_f(E,M) → RΓ(E,M) → ⊕_{w ∈ Sp} RΓ(E_w,M^−_w), whence 0 → H^0(G_{E,Sp},M) → ⊕_{w ∈ Sp}H^0(E_w,M^−_w) → H̃^1_f(E,M) → H^1_f(E,M) → 0, with H^1_f(E,M) := Ker(H^1(G_{E,Sp},M) → ⊕_w H^1(E_w,M^−_w)) the Greenberg Selmer group.
items.locator: §5.3.2 with displays (5.3.1)–(5.3.3), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (after Nekovář, Selmer complexes)

items.name: Perfectness of the Selmer complex over the base
items.statement: Proposition 5.3.2. The Selmer complex R̃Γ_f(E,M) and all terms of the exact triangle belong to D^{[0,3]}_{perf}(_{O_X}Mod).
items.locator: Proposition 5.3.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Nekovář's p-adic height pairing over a base and its specialisation
items.statement: Given strict Greenberg data M, M^ι over X and a perfect pairing M ⊗_{O_X} M^ι → O_X(1) of O_X[G_{E,Sp}]-modules under which M^+_w and M^{+,ι}_w are exact orthogonals, and a profinite abelian Γ_F, Nekovář's construction gives h_M : H̃^1_f(E,M) ⊗_{O_X} H̃^1_f(E,M^ι) → O_X ⊗̂ Γ_F. Proposition 5.3.3: for a regular x ∈ X and P_1 ⊗ P_2, h_{M ⊗ κ(x)}(P_{1,x},P_{2,x}) = (h_M(P_1,P_2))(x).
items.locator: §5.3.3 with display (5.3.4) and Proposition 5.3.3, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Nekovář, Selmer complexes, §11.1; Venerucci, thesis, Appendix C, Lemma 0.16)

items.name: Venerucci's conormal-valued height pairing and its symmetry
items.statement: For a local complete intersection Y ⊂ X with restricted data M_Y^?, there is a height pairing h_{M_Y/M_X} : H̃^1_f(E,M_Y) ⊗_{O_Y} H̃^1_f(E,M_Y^ι) → 𝓝^*_{Y/X}. Proposition 5.3.4: (1) if Γ_F is a profinite abelian quotient of G_{E,Sp}, X = Y ⊗̂_{Spec Q_p} Spec Z_p⟦Γ_F⟧_{Q_p} and M^?_X = M^?_Y ⊗ Z_p⟦Γ_F⟧ with the tautological character (resp. its inverse), then h_{M_Y/M_X} = h_{M_Y}; (2) if an involution ι of X stabilises Y with M^ι_X = M_X ⊗_{O_X,ι}O_X and likewise for the M^+_{X,w}, if the duality is ε-hermitian, if d_{Y/X}ι = ε' id on 𝓝^*_{Y/X} and if there is an O_Y-linear isomorphism c : H̃^1_f(E,M^ι_Y) → H̃^1_f(E,M_Y), then (z,z') ↦ h_{M_Y/M_X}(z,cz') is εε'-symmetric. In the application Y = X, X = X^♯, M_Y = 𝓥, M_X = 𝓥^♯, and h_{𝓥/𝓥^♯} = ½ h_𝓥.
items.locator: §5.3.3 with displays (5.3.5)–(5.3.6) and Proposition 5.3.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Venerucci, thesis, Appendix C, §0.21)

items.name: Tate 0-cycles with coefficients in a local system
items.statement: For a variety X/E and an étale local system 𝓦 of R[G_E]-modules, 𝓩_0(X,𝓦) := ⊕_{x ∈ X closed} H^0(x,𝓦) with H^0(x,𝓦) := H^0(x̄,𝓦)^{G_E}; elements are written Σ_{x̄'}[x̄'] ⊗ ξ_{x̄'}. For dim X = 0 the fundamental class is [X] := Σ_{x̄' ∈ X(Ē)}[x̄'] ⊗ 1; the support |a| of a Tate cycle is the support of the divisor Σ[x̄'] over the x̄' with ξ_{x̄'} ≠ 0. For 𝓦 = R, 𝓩_0(X,R) is the usual module of 0-cycles and CH_0(X,R) its quotient by rational equivalence.
items.locator: §6.1.1 (Tate cycles), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The e-Abel–Jacobi map of a Tate 0-cycle on a curve
items.statement: For a Tate cycle a on a curve X with class cl̄(a) ∈ H^2(X̄,𝓦(1)) and a Galois-equivariant idempotent e acting on the right with cl̄(a)e = 0, applying e to 0 → H^1(X̄,𝓦(1)) → H^1(X̄−|a|,𝓦(1)) → H^2_{|a|}(X̄,𝓦(1)) → H^2(X̄,𝓦(1)) and pulling back along a gives an extension 0 → H^1(X̄,𝓦(1))e → E_a → R → 0 of G_E-representations; AJ e : 𝓩_0(X,𝓦) → H^1(G_E, H_1(X̄,𝓦)e) sends a to its class. For 𝓦 = R and e acting by correspondences it factors through CH_0(X,R)e.
items.locator: §6.1.2 (Abel–Jacobi map), displays (6.1.1)–(6.1.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)
items.note: GH.1 plans the étale Abel–Jacobi map from the cycle class and the Hochschild–Serre filtration, including independence of choices; the coefficient-system and support-localisation form used here is its curve case with a projector.

items.name: CM cycles on Z_K with coefficients, and the Hodge modification
items.statement: For V' ⊂ H'(A^∞) and K ⊂ (G×H)'(A^∞) with K ∩ H'(A^∞) ⊇ V, the diagonal e'_{V',K} : Y'_{V'} → Z_K is y ↦ [(e(ỹ),ỹ)]. If W satisfies (wt) then W^{H'} is a line, and any ξ ∈ W^{H'} gives Q_p → e'^*𝓦, whence pushforwards e'_{W,K,V',*} : 𝓩_0(Y'_{V'},Z_p) → 𝓩_0(Z_K,𝓦^∘) ⊗ W^∨_{H'}. One sets Δ_{W,(K,V')} := e'_{W,K,V,*}[Y'_{V'}] and Δ^∘_{W,(K,V')} := |Y'_{V'}(Ē)|^{−1}Δ_{W,(K,V')} for W ≠ Q_p, while for W = Q_p one takes Δ^∘_{(K,V')} := |Y'_{V'}(Ē)|^{−1}(Δ_{(K,V')} − deg(Δ_{(K,V')})·ξ_Hodge) in CH_0(Z_K)_{Q_p}, with ξ_Hodge the Hodge class.
items.locator: §6.2.1–§6.2.2 with display (6.2.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Compatibility under pushforward and homological triviality of the CM cycle
items.statement: Lemma 6.2.1. The image of Δ^∘_{W,(K'',V'')} under pushforward in 𝓩_0(Z_K,𝓦) (or CH_0(Z_K)_{Q_p} when W = Q_p) is independent of V'', K'' with V'' ⊂ K'' ∩ H'(A^∞) and K' ⊂ K, and cl̄(Δ^∘_{W,(K,V')}) = 0 in H^2(Z̄_K,𝓦(1)).
items.locator: Lemma 6.2.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The Heegner classes P_W, P_Π and P^{ord}_Π
items.statement: P_{W,(K,V')} := AJ(Δ^∘_{W,(K,V')}) ∈ H^1(G_{E,Sp}, H_1(Z̄_K,𝓦)); these are compatible under pushforward and give P_W ∈ lim_K H^1(G_{E,Sp},H_1(Z̄_K,𝓦)), invariant under H'(A^∞). Via Carayol's injection Π ↪ colim_K Hom_{L[G_E]}(𝓗_1(Z̄_K,𝓦),V_Π) and biduality, P_W yields for each ordinary Π of weight W a map P_Π : Π → H^1(G_{E,Sp},V_Π), whose restriction to Π_{H'_∞} is the functional of the introduction, and P^{ord}_Π := P_Π γ^{ord}_{H'} : Π^{ord} → H^1(G_{E,Sp},V_Π).
items.locator: §1.2.4 with display (1.2.3), and §6.2.3 with displays (6.2.2)–(6.2.3), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Conjecture on the geometric origin of the Heegner classes
items.statement: Remark 6.2.2. It is conjectured that (i) there are a variety N_{W,(K,V')}/E of odd dimension 2d_W+1, a homologically trivial cycle 𝔷_{W,(K,V')} ∈ CH_{d_W}(N_{W,(K,V')})_0 and a map λ : H^{2d_W+1}(N̄_{W,(K,V')},Q_p(d+1)) → H_1(Z̄_K,𝓦) with P_{W,(K,V')} = λ(AJ(𝔷)); and (ii) the classes P_{W,(K,V')} lie in H^1_f(E,H_1(Z̄_K,𝓦)), so that P_Π takes values in H^1_f(E,V_Π). For G = GL_{2/Q}, (i) holds with a Kuga–Sato variety, generalising Nekovář's Proposition II.2.4; the obstruction in general is that Z is not of PEL type when F ≠ Q.
items.locator: Remark 6.2.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The universal Heegner class 𝓟_W
items.statement: Definition 6.3.1. With d_r := |Y'_r(Ē)|, d^∘ = d_r ∏_{v|p}q_v^{−r_v} ∈ Z_{≥1} and M^∘_{K^{p}{}',W} = lim_r 𝓗_1(Z̄_{W,r},𝓦^∘)^{ord}, the universal Heegner point of weight W is 𝓟_W := P_W γ^{ord}_{H'} ∈ d^{∘,−1}H^1(G_{E,Sp},M^∘_{K^p,W}), where γ^{ord}_{H'} : lim_{K_p}𝓗_1(Z̄_{K^{p}{}'K_p},𝓦)^{H'(A)} → M_{K^{p}{}',W} is the operator of Proposition A.2.4. One writes 𝓟 := 𝓟_{Q_p}.
items.locator: Definition 6.3.1 with display (6.3.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Independence of the universal Heegner class from the weight
items.statement: Proposition 6.3.2. Under the identification H^1(E,M^∘_{K^{p}{}'} ⊗_{Z_p}O_L) ≅ H^1(E,M^∘_{K^{p}{}',W}) induced by the isomorphism j_W of Proposition 3.1.2(2), one has j_{W,*}(𝓟) = 𝓟_W.
items.locator: Proposition 6.3.2 with display (6.3.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (using Lemma A.4.2)

items.name: Vanishing of the local cohomology away from p at classical points
items.statement: Lemma 6.4.1. For z ∈ X^{cl} with V = 𝓥_{|z} and a place w ∤ p of E, H^i(E_w,V) = 0 for all i.
items.locator: Lemma 6.4.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Bloch–Kato and Greenberg Selmer groups agree at classical points of regular weight
items.statement: Lemma 6.4.2. If Π_z satisfies (wt) then H^1_{f,BK}(E,V) = H^1_{f,Gr}(E,V), where the left side is defined by the Bloch–Kato local conditions at all w ∈ Sp and the right side by the ordinary filtration.
items.locator: Lemma 6.4.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Support of the local cohomology sheaves away from p
items.statement: Lemma 6.4.3. For a finite place w ∤ p of E the sheaves H^1(E_w,𝓥) and H^1(E_w,𝓜^{H'_Σ}_{K^{p}{}'}) are supported in a closed subset of X (resp. X^{(3)}) disjoint from X^{cl}; one writes X^{(3,w)} ⊃ X^{cl} for the open complement in X^{(3)} of the support of H^1(E_w,𝓥).
items.locator: Lemma 6.4.3 with display (6.4.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Vanishing of the singular localisation of 𝓟 at the places above p
items.statement: Lemma 6.4.4. For a place w | p of E the image loc^−_w(𝓟) of 𝓟 in H^1(E_w, 𝓜^{H'_Σ,−}_{K^{p}{}',w}) vanishes over X^{(3)}. (The proof twists by a square root of the determinant, writes the maximal pro-p abelian extension E_∞/E as an increasing union of E_n totally ramified at p, applies Howard's argument at the finite levels, and passes to the limit by Lemma 5.2.2.)
items.locator: Lemma 6.4.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Howard, Variation of Heegner points in Hida families, proof of Proposition 2.4.5, primes v | p)

items.name: The universal class is a section of the Selmer sheaf
items.statement: Corollary 6.4.5. With X^{(3,f)} := ∩_{w ∈ S}X^{(3,w)} ⊃ X^{cl}, the class 𝓟 defines a section 𝓟 ∈ H̃^1_f(E,𝓜^{H'_Σ}_{K^{p}{}'})(X^{(3,f)}) = H^1_f(E,𝓜^{H'_Σ}_{K^{p}{}'})(X^{(3,f)}).
items.locator: Corollary 6.4.5, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The exceptional locus of a Hida family
items.statement: For w | v | p let μ^±_w : E_w^× → O(X)^× be the characters giving the Galois action on 𝓥^±. X^{exc,v} ⊂ X is the closed subset where μ^−_w = 1 for some (equivalently every) w | v; X^{exc} := ∪_{v|p}X^{exc,v}, X^{cl,exc,(v)} := X^{cl} ∩ X^{exc,(v)} and X^{cl,n-exc,(v)} := X^{cl} − X^{cl,exc,(v)}. A representation Π = Π_{|z} is exceptional at v if z ∈ X^{exc,v}.
items.locator: §6.4.7 with display (6.4.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Characterisation of exceptional representations and the exceptional defect
items.statement: Lemma 6.4.6. For an ordinary Π = π ⊗ χ over a p-adic field with weights w̲, l̲: (1) for v | p the following are equivalent: Π is exceptional at v; e_v(V_{(π,χ)}) = 0; π_v is special of the form St ⊗ α_v, χ_w·α_v∘N_{E_w/F_v} = 1 for some (all) w | v, and w_σ = 2, l_σ = 0 for all σ inducing v. (2) With S_p^{exc} = S_p^{exc,s} ⊔ S_p^{exc,ns} the set of exceptional places (split, resp. nonsplit in E): (a) the kernel of H̃^1_f(E,V_Π) ↠ H^1_f(E,V_Π) has dimension 2|S_p^{exc,s}| + |S_p^{exc,ns}|; (b) if B is split at all v | p then ε^G_v(V_Π) = −1 ⟺ v ∈ S_p^{exc,ns}.
items.locator: Lemma 6.4.6, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Heegner classes lie in the Bloch–Kato Selmer group
items.statement: Proposition 6.4.7. If Π is not exceptional, or has trivial weight, then P_Π takes values in H^1_f(E,V_Π) ⊂ H^1(G_{E,Sp},V_Π). (For non-exceptional Π this follows from Corollary 6.4.5, Theorem C and Lemma A.2.5: ∂P_Π γ^{ord}_{H'} = 0 and γ^{ord}_{H'} is not annihilated.)
items.locator: Proposition 6.4.7, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The enhanced ordinary Heegner class
items.statement: For z = (x,y) ∈ X^{cl} with representation Π, P̃^{ord}_Π := 𝓟_{|z} ∈ H̃^1_f(E,V_Π); its image under H̃^1_f(E,V_Π) → H^1_f(E,V_Π) is P^{ord}_Π, and by Lemma 6.4.6 that map fails to be an isomorphism precisely when Π is exceptional.
items.locator: §6.4.8 with display (6.4.3), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The cyclotomic space 𝓔_Z and the Galois group Γ_F
items.statement: Γ_F := F^×_{A^∞}/F^× Ô^{p,×}_F, identified by class field theory with the Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of F unramified outside p, and 𝓔_{Z/L} := Spec(Z_p⟦Γ_F⟧_L); a point s ∈ 𝓔_{Z/L} is a p-adic character χ_{F,s} of Γ_F, s = 0 being the trivial character. The p-adic cyclotomic character of a number field E is χ_{cyc,E} = χ_{cyc,Q}∘N_{E/Q} with χ_{cyc,Q}(x) = |x|_{A^∞}⟨x_p⟩_p.
items.locator: §1.1.2 and §1.6 (Notation), display (1.6.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The p-adic and archimedean interpolation factors e_v, e_∞, e_{p∞}
items.statement: With γ(W,ψ_v)^{−1} = L(W)/(ε(W,ψ_v)L(W^*(1))) the inverse Deligne–Langlands factor, ψ the standard additive character, ψ_{E,w} = ψ_v ∘ Tr_{E_w/F_v}, ad(V_{π,v})(1)^{++} := Hom(V^−_{π,v},V^+_{π,v}) and d_v a generator of the different: e_v(V_{(π_x,χ_y)}) := |d_v|^{−1/2}·(∏_{w|v}γ(ιWD(V^+_{π,v|G_{E,w}} ⊗ V_{χ,w}),ψ_{E,w})^{−1})/(γ(ιWD(ad(V_{π,v})(1))^{++},ψ_v)^{−1})·𝓛(V_{(π^ι,χ^ι),v})^{−1}; e_∞ := i^{(w+l)[F:Q]} and e_{p∞} := e_∞·∏_{v|p}e_v. When w+l = 0 these lie in ι Q_p(x_0,y_0) and one sets e_{p∞}(V_{(π,χ)}) := ι^{−1}e_{p∞}(V_{(π^ι,χ^ι)}).
items.locator: §1.4.2 with displays (1.4.1)–(1.4.4), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Fontaine's functor ιWD; Tate's normalisations of L- and ε-factors)

items.name: The multivariable p-adic L-function on the Hida family
items.statement: Theorem 1.4.1. There is a meromorphic function 𝓛_p(𝓥^♯) ∈ 𝓚(X^♯_0) on the ordinary eigenvariety for G_0 × H, whose polar locus 𝒟 does not meet X^{cl}_0, uniquely characterised by: for every z = (x,y) ∈ X^{♯,cl}_0(C) − 𝒟(C) corresponding to π_x ⊗ χ_y of weights (w̲_x,l̲_y) with |l_{y,σ}| < w_{x,σ} and |w_x+l_y| ≤ w_{x,σ} − |l_{y,σ}| − 2 for all σ, 𝓛_p(𝓥)(x,y) = e_{p∞}(V_{(π_x,χ_y)})·𝓛(V_{(π_x,χ_y)},0), the product over all places of the normalised local factors.
items.locator: Theorem 1.4.1 with display (1.4.5), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024); Disegni, p-adic L-functions via local-global interpolation: the case of GL_2 × GU(1), Canad. J. Math.

items.name: The cyclotomic p-adic L-function of V and its derivative
items.statement: For an ordinary Hilbert modular form π_0 and a Hecke character χ of E, 𝓛_p(V_{(π_0,χ)},s) := 𝓛_p(𝓥^♯)(z_s) ∈ 𝓚(𝓔_{Z/L}), where z_s is the family V_{π|G_E} ⊗ χχ_{F,s|G_E}. If ε(V) = −1 then 𝓛_p(V_{(π_0,χ)},0) = 0 and one writes 𝓛'_p(V_{(π_0,χ)},0) = d𝓛_p(V_{(π_0,χ)})(0) ∈ T_0𝓔_{Z/L} = Γ_F ⊗̂ L. The normal derivative along X_0 ⊂ X^♯_0 is d^♯𝓛_p(𝓥) := d_{X_0/X^♯_0}𝓛_p(𝓥^♯) ∈ 𝓚(X_0) ⊗̂ Γ_F.
items.locator: §1.1.2, display (1.1.1), and §1.4.3, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The p-adic height pairings on V and on the Hida family
items.statement: For ordinary π the restriction V_w is reducible, 0 → V^+_w → V_w → V^−_w → 0, with V^+_w and V^{ι,+}_w exact orthogonals under a fixed V ⊗ V^ι → L(1); this gives h_V : H̃^1_f(E,V) ⊗ H̃^1_f(E,V^ι) → L ⊗̂ Γ_F. Over a locally distinguished Hida family the dualities 𝓥 ⊗ 𝓥^ι → O_X(1) interpolate this, and together with the deformation to a Hida family X^♯ for G × H give h_{𝓥/𝓥^♯} : H̃^1_f(E,𝓥) ⊗_{O_X} H̃^1_f(E,𝓥^ι) → 𝓝^*_{X/X^♯} ≅ O_X ⊗̂ Γ_F. For trivial W the pairing h_V agrees with the p-adic height pairings on abelian varieties in the literature.
items.locator: §1.2.7 with displays (1.2.9)–(1.2.11) and §1.4.1 with displays (1.4.6)–(1.4.7), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Condition (★) of the Correction
items.statement: Let S_{p,ns} be the set of p-adic places of F that are nonsplit in E. A Hecke character χ of E satisfies (★) if for each v ∈ S_{p,ns} the place v is inert in E and χ_v is unramified. This is the hypothesis under which the corrected form of [Disegni, The p-adic Gross–Zagier formula on Shimura curves, II: nonsplit primes] proves the trivial-weight p-adic Gross–Zagier formula, and it is therefore required in Theorems A, B and B^ord.
items.locator: Appendix B (Correction), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Hida* families
items.statement: Assume no p-adic place of F is ramified in E. Define M^*_{K^p} as M_{K^p} in §1.3.1 but with the limit taken only over subgroups K_p containing N_{G,0} × ∏_{v ∈ S_{p,ns}}O^×_{E,v}, and 𝓔^{ord,*}_{K^p} as 𝓔^{ord}_{K^p} with M_{K^p} replaced by M^*_{K^p}; equivalently 𝓔^{ord,*}_{K^p} is the closure of the set of classical points of 𝓔^{ord}_{K^p} corresponding to representations satisfying (★). A Hida* family for (G×H)' is an irreducible component of 𝓔^{ord,*}_{K^p}. Theorems D and E hold for Hida* families rather than Hida families.
items.locator: Appendix B (Correction), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Theorem A: the p-adic Beilinson–Bloch–Kato conjecture in analytic rank one
items.statement: Theorem A, as corrected. Let π_0 be a Hilbert modular form over L of weight w̲ and χ a Hecke character of E over L of weight l̲, V := V_{π_0|G_E} ⊗ V_χ, and assume (wt) |l_σ| < w_σ for all σ; (sd) ω_{π_0}ω_χ = 1; (ε) ε(V) = −1; (ord) π_0 is ordinary; (n-exc) V is not exceptional; and, by the Correction, (★). Then (1) 𝓛'_p(V_{(π_0,χ)},0) ≠ 0 ⟹ dim_L H̃^1_f(E,V) ≥ 1, with an explicit nonzero element of H̃^1_f(E,V) = H^1_f(E,V) whose p-adic height is also nonzero; (2) for a stable lattice T ⊂ V, if moreover the conditions of [Fouquet, Theorem B(i)] hold, then (a) dim_L H̃^1_f(E,V) = 1 and (b) 𝓛'_p(V_{(π_0,χ)},0) ⪰_{Z_p} R_T·|H̃^2_f(E,T)_tors| in L ⊗̂ Γ_F, where R_T is the regulator of the height pairing on H̃^1_f(E,T) ⊗ H̃^1_f(E,T^*(1)). Here m_1 ⪰_A m_2 means m_1 ⊆ m_2.
items.locator: Theorem A (§1.1.3), with the hypothesis (★) added in Appendix B, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: A variant of Theorem A for self-dual Hilbert modular forms
items.statement: Suppose π_0 is ordinary with ω_{π_0} = 1 and ε(V_{π_0}) = −1, that either [F:Q] is odd or π_{0,v} is not a principal series for some v ∤ p∞, and that π_{0,v} is not Steinberg for any v | p. If L'_p(V_{π_0},0) ≠ 0 for Dimitrov's p-adic L-function, then conclusions (1) and (2)(a) of Theorem A hold with (E,V) replaced by (F,V_{π_0}); the proof chooses an auxiliary CM extension E and reduces to Theorem A.
items.locator: §1.1.4 (A variant for selfdual Hilbert modular forms), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Dimitrov, Automorphic symbols, p-adic L-functions and ordinary cohomology of Hilbert modular varieties)

items.name: Theorem B: the p-adic Gross–Zagier formula for arbitrary weight
items.statement: Theorem B, as corrected. Let Π = π ⊗ χ be an ordinary, locally distinguished, non-exceptional automorphic representation of (G×H)'(A) over L satisfying (★), and V = V_Π. Then the image of P_Π lies in H^1_f(E,V) and, for f_1 ∈ Π_{H'_∞}, f_2 ∈ Π^∨_{H'_∞}, f_3 ∈ Π, f_4 ∈ Π^∨ with (f_3,f_4)_Π ≠ 0, h_V(P_Π(f_1),P_{Π^∨}(f_2))/(f_3,f_4)_Π = e_{p∞}(V_{(π,χ)})^{−1}·𝓛'_p(V_{(π,χ)},0)·Q(f_1⊗f_2/f_3⊗f_4).
items.locator: Theorem B (§1.2.8), with (★) added in Appendix B, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Theorem B^ord: the p-adic Gross–Zagier formula for ordinary forms
items.statement: Theorem B^ord, as corrected. Let Π = π ⊗ χ be an ordinary, locally distinguished representation of (G×H)'(A) over L satisfying (★) — exceptional Π allowed — with V = V_Π and P̃^{ord}_Π the enhanced Heegner class. Then for f_1 ∈ Π^{ord}_{H'_∞}, f_2 ∈ Π^{∨,ord}_{H'_∞}, f_3 ∈ Π^{ord}, f_4 ∈ Π^{∨,ord} with (f_3,f_4)^{ord} ≠ 0, h_V(P̃^{ord}_Π(f_1),P̃^{ord}_{Π^∨}(f_2))/(f_3,f_4)^{ord}_Π = 𝓛'_p(V_{(π,χ)},0)·Q^{ord}(f_1⊗f_2/f_3⊗f_4).
items.locator: Theorem B^ord (§7.1.1) with display (7.1.1), and Appendix B, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Equivalence of Theorem B and Theorem B^ord in the non-exceptional case
items.statement: Lemma 7.1.2. If Π is not exceptional then Theorem B^ord is equivalent to Theorem B. (The comparison uses Proposition 4.3.4 and the nondegeneracy of the ordinary pairing.)
items.locator: Lemma 7.1.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Comparison with the one-variable p-adic L-function at a point of trivial weight
items.statement: Lemma 7.1.3. For z = (x,y) of weights (0;(2,…,2)) and (0;(0,…,0)), with A the modular abelian variety attached to π_{0,x} and 𝓛_p(V_{(A,χ)}) the p-adic L-function of [Disegni, nonsplit primes, Theorem A], the pullback of 𝓛_p(𝓥^♯) along j_{(x,y)} : 𝓔_Z → {x} × 𝓔^{ord}_H, χ_F ↦ π_{0,x} ⊗ χ_y·χ_{F∘N_{E_A^×/F_A^×}}, equals 𝓛_p(V_{(A,χ)}).
items.locator: Lemma 7.1.3 with display (7.1.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Density of the classical points of trivial weight satisfying (p-crys), in a Hida* family
items.statement: Lemma 7.1.4, as corrected. In a Hida* family, the classical points of trivial weight that satisfy (p-crys) — that is, V_{x|G_{F_v}} potentially crystalline for all v | p, equivalently π_{x,v} a principal series — are dense. The last paragraph of the printed proof of Lemma 7.1.4 applies verbatim. Condition (ram), the sufficient ramification of χ_{y,p}, is no longer relevant, because the corrected [nonsplit, Theorem B] does not require it.
items.locator: Lemma 7.1.4 (printed form, §7.1.3) and Appendix B (Correction), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The equivalence of the universal and the pointwise formulas
items.statement: Proposition 7.1.5. Let X' = X'_{K^{p}{}'} := X^{(6)} ∩ X^{(3,f)} ⊃ X^{cl}. The following are equivalent: (1) Theorem D holds over X'_{K^{p}{}'} for all K^{p}{}' ⊂ K^p; (2a) Theorem B^ord holds at all points of X^{cl} satisfying (wt); (2b) Theorem B^ord holds at all points of X^{cl,p-crys,Q_p,ram}; (3a) Theorem B holds at all points of X^{cl,n-exc} satisfying (wt); (3b) Theorem B holds at all points of X^{cl,p-crys,Q_p,ram}. The specialisation input is that the conormal map 𝓝^*_{X/X^♯} → 𝓝^*_{X/X×𝓔_Z} is multiplication by ½, so h_𝓥 specialises to ½h_V and d^♯𝓛_p(𝓥) to ½𝓛'_p(V,0).
items.locator: Proposition 7.1.5 with §7.1.3, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Theorem C: the universal Heegner class and Howard's question
items.statement: Theorem C (not affected by the Correction). Let X be a locally distinguished Hida family for (G×H)'.
