There are an open X' ⊂ X containing X^{cl} and a map 𝓟_{K^{p}{}'} : Π^{K^{p}{}',ord}_{H'_Σ} → H^1_f(G_{E,Sp},𝓥) of sheaves over X' such that (1) 𝓟_{K^{p}{}'} is invariant under the away-from-pΣ Hecke algebra of H'; (2) for every z ∈ X^{cl} whose representation Π_z satisfies (wt), 𝓟_{K^{p}{}'|z} = P^{ord}_{Π_z,K^{p}{}'} under the natural map H^1(G_{E,Sp},𝓥)_{|z} → H^1(G_{E,Sp},V_{Π_z}). Part (2) answers, in this generality, Howard's question whether his big class interpolates Heegner cycles at all classical points.
items.locator: Theorem C (§1.3.3) proved in §6.4.6, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Theorem D: the universal p-adic Gross–Zagier formula
items.statement: Theorem D, as corrected: for Hida* families. Let X be a locally distinguished Hida* family for (G×H)', Π^{(ι)} := Π^{K^{p}{}',ord,(ι)}_{H'_Σ}, O := O_X, 𝓚 := 𝓚_X. Then there is an open X' ⊂ X containing X^{cl} over which all the constructions can be made and h_{𝓥/𝓥^♯}(𝓟(f_1),𝓟^ι(f_2))/((f_3,f_4)) = d^♯𝓛_p(𝓥^♯)·𝓠(f_1⊗f_2/f_3⊗f_4), an equality of 𝓚 ⊗̂_{Z_p}Γ_F-valued O-linear functionals on (Π ⊗_O Π^ι) ⊗_{O^×}(Π ⊗_O Π^ι)^{×,−1}. The formula also holds at exceptional classical points, in the form of Theorem B^ord.
items.locator: Theorem D (§1.4.3), with Hida* in place of Hida by Appendix B, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Theorem E: an Iwasawa main conjecture for derivatives
items.statement: Theorem E, as corrected: for Hida* families. Let X be a locally distinguished Hida* family for (G×H)' satisfying the further conditions of [Fouquet, Theorem B(iii)], X' the open subset of Theorem D, which may be assumed regular, and 𝓡 ⊂ O_{X'} ⊗̂ Γ_F the regulator of the height pairing h_{𝓥/𝓥^♯} over X'. Then d^♯𝓛_p(𝓥) ⪰_{O_{X'}} 𝓡·char_{O_{X'}}(H̃^2_f(E,𝓥)_{O_{X'}-tors}).
items.locator: Theorem E (§1.5.1), with Hida* in place of Hida by Appendix B, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Theorem F: generic non-vanishing of p-adic heights for self-dual CM motives
items.statement: Theorem F (not affected by the Correction, since its hypotheses force S_{p,ns} = ∅). Let 𝓔^{ord,sd}_H ⊂ 𝓔^{ord}_H be the closed subspace cut out by χ_{|F_A^×} = η·χ_{cyc,F}, a torsor under 𝓔^{ord}_{H'}, smooth of dimension [F:Q], and let Y ⊂ 𝓔^{ord,sd}_H be an irreducible component of type −1, i.e. with ε(1,χ_x) = −1 for all x ∈ Y^{cl}. Suppose every prime v | p of F splits in E, that E/F is ramified, and that p ∤ 2D_F h_E^−. Then there is a nonempty open Y' ⊂ Y such that for all y ∈ Y^{cl} ∩ Y', H^1_f(E,χ_y) ≠ 0 and the p-adic height pairing H^1_f(E,χ_y) ⊗ H^1_f(E,χ_y^{−1}(1)) → Q_p(y) ⊗̂ Γ_F is non-vanishing.
items.locator: Theorem F (§1.5.2) proved in §7.1.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Theorem G: non-vanishing along an exceptional classical Hida family
items.statement: Theorem G (not affected by the Correction). Let X_0 be a Hida family for PGL_{2/Q}, X^♯_0 the Hida family for GL_{2/Q} containing it, and 𝓥_0, 𝓥^♯_0 the associated rank-two G_Q-representations. Suppose X_0 contains a point corresponding to an elliptic curve A with split multiplicative reduction at p and L(A,1) ≠ 0. Then (1) a universal Heegner class 𝓟_0 is non-vanishing along X_0; (2) H̃^1_f(Q,𝓥_0) has generic rank one, generated by 𝓟_0; (3) the p-adic height pairing h_{𝓥_0/𝓥^♯_0} is non-vanishing.
items.locator: Theorem G (§1.5.3) proved in §7.3.6, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Theorem H: a universal Waldspurger formula
items.statement: Theorem H. Let B be a totally definite quaternion algebra over F, G the associated coherent group, E ↪ B a fixed CM extension, and X a locally distinguished Hida family for (G×H)', whose Shimura varieties are all zero-dimensional. With 𝓟 : Π^{K^p,ord}_{H'_Σ} → O_X the universal toric period interpolating the P^{ord}_{Π_z}, ((,)) the interpolated pairing and 𝓠 as in §4.4, there is an open X' ⊂ X containing X^{cl} such that 𝓟(f_1)·𝓟^ι(f_2)/((f_3,f_4)) = 𝓛_p(𝓥^♯)_{|X}·𝓠(f_1⊗f_2/f_3⊗f_4), an equality of 𝓚-valued O-linear functionals. It follows from its specialisations at classical points satisfying (wt), which are known by modifying Waldspurger's formula as in Theorem B^ord.
items.locator: Theorem H (§7.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Pfaffian regulators of a skew-symmetric pairing
items.statement: Let L be a field of characteristic zero, M and T finite-dimensional L-spaces, h : M ⊗ M → T skew-symmetric, r = dim M. If r is even, Pf^+(M,h) ∈ (Sym^{r/2}T)/L^× is the Pfaffian of (h(x_i,x_j)) for any basis. If r is odd, the enhanced Pf^−(M,h) ∈ (M ⊗ Sym^{(r−1)/2}T)/L^× is defined by prescribing ∂^e Pf^− for every basis ∂_1,…,∂_d of T^∨ and every e with Σe_i = (r−1)/2: with I the support of e and M_I the sum over i ∈ I of the radicals of ∂_i h, one sets ∂^ePf^− := 0 if dim M_I ≥ 2 and ∂^ePf^−(M,h) := x ⊗ ∂^ePf^+(M̄,h̄) if dim M_I = 1 with generator x and M̄ = M/M_I. In the even case Pf^+(M,h)² is the discriminant R(M,h); in the odd case, given a symmetric h^♯ : M ⊗ M → T^♯, h^♯(Pf^−,Pf^−) is the image of the discriminant of h ⊕ h^♯. A lattice in M lifts the ambiguity to a unit.
items.locator: §7.3.1 with Remarks 7.3.1 and 7.3.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Conjecture Pf: leading terms of universal Heegner classes and toric periods
items.statement: Conjecture Pf. Let G be incoherent (ε := −1) or coherent totally definite (ε := +1), X a locally distinguished Hida family, z ∈ X^{cl} a classical point at which 𝓟 is defined on a neighbourhood, V = 𝓥_{|z}, h^∥ := h^□_{z/X} : H̃^1_f(E,V) ⊗ H̃^1_f(E,V) → T^*_zX the Nekovář–Venerucci height pairing twisted by the complex conjugation, which is skew-symmetric, and Pf^{∥,±}(V) := Pf^±(H̃^1_f(E,V),h^∥). Put r̃ := dim_L H̃^1_f(E,V). Then (−1)^{r̃} = ε, 𝓟 vanishes to order at least ⌊r̃/2⌋ at z, and for any generator ℘ of (Π^{ord})^{*,H'(A^{p∞})} and all f ∈ Π^{ord}, (d^∥_z)^{⌊r̃/2⌋}𝓟(f) = Pf^{∥,ε}(V)·℘(f) in [H̃^1_f(E,V)^{(1+ε)/2} ⊗ Sym^{⌊r̃/2⌋}T^*_zX]/Q_p(z)^×.
items.locator: Conjecture Pf (§7.3.2) with display (7.3.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The parity part of Conjecture Pf
items.statement: The parity statement (−1)^{r̃} = ε follows from Nekovář's parity theorem (−1)^r = ε(V) for r = dim H^1_f(E,V) together with Lemma 6.4.6(2): ε = ε(V)·(−1)^{r^{exc,ns}} and r̃ = r + 2r^{exc,s} + r^{exc,ns}, where r^{exc,s} and r^{exc,ns} count the exceptional places above p that are split, resp. nonsplit, in E.
items.locator: §7.3.4 with displays (7.3.2)–(7.3.3), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Nekovář, Selmer complexes, Theorem 12.2.3)

items.name: Comparison of Conjecture Pf with the Fornea–Gehrmann plectic invariants
items.statement: §7.3.5. Let A/F be a modular elliptic curve whose set of places of multiplicative reduction above p consists of r primes v_1,…,v_r inert in E, and assume Sha(A_E)[p^∞] finite, so that r̃ = r + r_A. Granting the conjectural relations of Fornea–Guitart–Masdeu for the element Q_A ∈ ⊗_i E_{v_i}^× ⊗̂ Q_p — namely that ℓ^a_{exc,⊗}(Q_A) vanishes unless r_A = r and r_A^+ + r^+ = r, in which case it is the determinant of (x̂^a_{i,v_j}) — Theorem A of Fornea–Gehrmann, (d^a_z)^r𝓟(f^∘) ≐ ℓ^a_{exc,⊗}(Q_A), is equivalent to the anticyclotomic projection of Conjecture Pf. The verification uses the explicit description H̃^1_f(E,V) = H^1_f(E,V) ⊕ ⊕_i Q_p[q_{v_i}] with h^a(q_v,q_{v'}) = 0 and h^a(x,q_v) = log^a_{A,v}(x̂_v), the isotropy of the ±-eigenspaces for the complex conjugation, and pf(0 M; −M^T 0) = ±det M.
items.locator: §7.3.5 with displays (7.3.4)–(7.3.6), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Fornea–Gehrmann, Plectic Stark–Heegner points, Theorem A; Fornea–Guitart–Masdeu, Plectic p-adic invariants, Conjectures 1.3 and 1.5)

items.name: A new proof of the Greenberg–Stevens exceptional-zero formula
items.statement: Remark 7.3.4. Combining Theorem D — or rather Theorem B^ord, whose hypothesis (★) holds in this setting because p is inert in E and χ = 1 is unramified — with the precise form of the identity h_{𝓥_0/𝓥^♯_0}(𝓟_0,𝓟_0^ι)(x_0) = c·ℓ(q)·L(A_E,1)/Ω_{A_E} gives a new proof of the theorem of Greenberg–Stevens: for an elliptic curve A/Q with split multiplicative reduction at p and p-adic L-function L_p(V_pA) ∈ Z_p⟦Γ_Q⟧_{Q_p}, L'_p(V_pA,0) = (ℓ(q)/ord_p(q))·L(A,1)/Ω_A.
items.locator: Remark 7.3.4 with display (7.3.7), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Greenberg–Stevens, Invent. Math. 111 (1993), 407–447)

items.name: The Bertolini–Darmon rigid-analytic Gross–Zagier formula at an exceptional point
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem G, with E imaginary quadratic in which p is inert, the primes dividing the conductor of A split, and L(A,η,1) ≠ 0, so that A has split multiplicative reduction over E with Tate parameter q ∈ E_p^×, there is c ∈ Q_p^× with 𝓟_{0,E}(x_0) ⊗ 𝓟_{0,E}^ι(x_0) = c·(L(A_E,1)/Ω_{A_E})·[q] ⊗ [q] in H̃^1_f(Q,V_pA_E)^{⊗2}. Combined with Nekovář's Kolyvagin method this gives generic rank one, and with the Barré-Sirieix–Diaz–Gramain–Philibert theorem (q is not a root of unity times an algebraic number, so ℓ(q) ≠ 0) it gives the non-vanishing of the height.
items.locator: §7.3.6 with display (7.3.7), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Bertolini–Darmon, Ann. of Math. 146 (1997), 111–147, as reformulated in their survey, Theorem 5.4; Nekovář, Kolyvagin's method for Chow groups of Kuga–Sato varieties; Barré-Sirieix–Diaz–Gramain–Philibert)

items.name: Nekovář's Kolyvagin method for Chow groups of Kuga–Sato varieties
items.statement: A non-vanishing Heegner-type class in the Selmer group of a modular Galois representation over an imaginary quadratic field bounds the Selmer rank by one; the paper applies this to deduce that H̃^1_f(Q,𝓥_0) has generic rank one once 𝓟_0 is shown to be non-vanishing.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Theorem G, §7.3.6, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Nekovář, Kolyvagin's method for Chow groups of Kuga–Sato varieties, Invent. Math. 107 (1992), 99–125)
items.note: GH.5 plans the higher-weight Kolyvagin system and its arithmetic hypotheses, that is Nekovář's method for Chow groups of Kuga–Sato varieties; HE.6 the clean rank-one descent it specialises to.

items.name: Fouquet's dihedral Iwasawa theory for nearly ordinary quaternionic automorphic forms
items.statement: For a nearly ordinary quaternionic automorphic form over a totally real field and a CM extension E/F, under the hypotheses of [Fouquet, Theorem B]: (i) if a Heegner class is non-torsion then the Selmer group H̃^1_f(E,V) has dimension one and the characteristic ideal of H̃^2_f(E,T)_tors divides the index of the class; and (iii) the corresponding two-variable statement over a Hida family, bounding char(H̃^2_f(E,𝓥)_tors) in terms of the universal class. These are the Euler-system inputs of Theorems A(2) and E, and they generalise Kolyvagin's bounds on Tate–Shafarevich groups.
items.locator: Used in Theorem A(2) and Theorem E, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Fouquet, Dihedral Iwasawa theory of nearly ordinary quaternionic automorphic forms, Compos. Math. 149 (2013), 356–416, Theorem B)

items.name: Cornut–Vatsal non-vanishing of CM points in the anticyclotomic tower
items.statement: The results of Cornut–Vatsal on the geometric distribution of CM points in quaternionic Shimura towers imply that, under mild conditions, the universal class 𝓟 is non-torsion over X.
items.locator: Remark 1.3.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Cornut–Vatsal, CM points and quaternion algebras, Doc. Math. 10 (2005), 263–309)
items.note: HE.8 plans exactly the geometric CM-point distribution and non-vanishing inputs of Cornut–Vatsal in the modular and quaternionic setting, and HE.8c pins their hypotheses over a totally real base.

items.name: The Katz p-adic L-function of a CM field
items.statement: For each p-adic CM type Σ of E and each connected component Y^♯ of 𝓔^{ord}_H there is L_Σ ∈ O(Y^♯), characterised by its values at the points y whose algebraic part is t ↦ ∏_{σ ∈ Σ}σ(t)^w σ(t/t^c)^{k_σ} with either w ≥ 1, or w < 1 and w+k_σ > 0 for all σ ∈ Σ, the value being related to L(1,χ_y). For a given y ∈ 𝓔^{ord,sd}_H there is a unique Σ whose interpolation range contains y, and one writes L_p(χ_y,s) := L_Σ(y(s)).
items.locator: Used in the proof of Theorem F, §7.1.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Katz, p-adic L-functions for CM fields, Invent. Math. 49 (1978), 199–297; Hida–Tilouine)
items.note: L3 plans Katz's p-adic L-function on the actual Hecke-character space of a CM field with a p-ordinary CM type, with the CM periods, the Eisenstein measure and the comparison of CM evaluations with critical Hecke L-values.

items.name: Non-vanishing of the normal derivative of the Katz p-adic L-function
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem F — all v | p split in E, E/F ramified, p ∤ 2D_F h_E^− — the normal derivative d^♯L_Σ ∈ 𝓝^*_{Y/Y^♯} of the Katz p-adic L-function along the self-dual subvariety is non-vanishing; Y'_Σ denotes the complement of its zero locus.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Theorem F, §7.1.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Burungale, On the μ-invariant of the cyclotomic derivative of a Katz p-adic L-function, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 14 (2015), 131–148)

items.name: Hsieh's non-vanishing of the anticyclotomic Katz L-function
items.statement: For a suitable component Y_2 ⊂ 𝓔^{ord,sd}_H the restriction L_{Σc|Y_2} is non-vanishing, which together with the density of classical points of a given weight produces a classical y' with L(1,χ') ≐ L_p(χ',0) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Theorem F, §7.1.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Hsieh, On the μ-invariant of anticyclotomic p-adic L-functions for CM fields, J. Reine Angew. Math. 688 (2014), 67–100)
items.note: L3h plans Hsieh's anticyclotomic square-root distribution for a Hilbert representation over a totally real field and a CM extension, with Theorem B's μ = 0 and its hypotheses; the non-vanishing used here is its consequence.

items.name: Hida's anticyclotomic main conjecture for self-dual Hecke characters of a CM field
items.statement: On a component Y_2 ⊂ 𝓔^{ord,sd}_H satisfying the hypotheses of [Hida, Quadratic exercises in Iwasawa theory], the anticyclotomic main conjecture holds, so that for a classical y' ∈ Y_2^{cl} the non-vanishing L_p(χ',0) ≠ 0 is equivalent to H^1_f(E,χ') = 0. Together with the sign-change lemma of Burungale–Disegni, which produces from a component of type −1 a component Y_2 of type +1 still satisfying Hida's hypotheses, and with the fact that an anticyclotomic character is of the form χ_0^c χ_0^{−1}, this supplies the claim in the proof of Theorem F.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Theorem F, §7.1.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Hida, Anticyclotomic main conjectures, Doc. Math. 2006, 465–532, and Quadratic exercises in Iwasawa theory, IMRN 2009, 912–952; Burungale–Disegni, Ann. Inst. Fourier 70 (2020), Lemma 2.5; Hida, Hilbert modular forms and Iwasawa theory, Lemma 5.3.1)

items.name: The Jacquet–Langlands correspondence and the map of eigenvarieties
items.statement: For appropriate tame levels there is a closed immersion ι_JL : 𝓔^{ord}_{G×H} → 𝓔^{ord}_{G_0×H} onto a union of irreducible components, induced by the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence between automorphic representations of the quaternionic group and of G_0 = Res_{F/Q}GL_2; locally, π_{x,v} = JL_v(π'_{x,v} ⊗ Q̄_p), and only special and supercuspidal representations lie in the image of JL_v.
items.locator: §1.4.2 and §3.3.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)
items.note: R17.1 plans the quaternionic local transfer with its image, and R17.3 the global Jacquet–Langlands correspondence; the induced map of ordinary eigenvarieties is their combination with PadicFamilies L5.

items.name: p-adic locally algebraic admissible representations
items.statement: Definition A.1.1. With G_p = G(Q_p) p-adically topologised, G_∞ = G(Q_p) with the Zariski topology, G = G_p × G_∞ and G_Δ the diagonal, a locally algebraic representation of G over L is a product of a smooth admissible representation of G_p and an algebraic representation of G_∞. For L/Q_p finite, such a Π is p-adic if for every compact open K ⊂ G_Δ there is a family of O_L-lattices Π^{K,∘} ⊂ Π^K with Π^{K',∘} ∩ Π^K = Π^{K,∘} for all K' ⊂ K. The typical example is colim_{K_p}H^i(Y_{K^pK_p},𝓦) ⊗ W^∨.
items.locator: Definition A.1.1 with §A.1.1 and display (A.1.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: p-adic locally algebraic coadmissible representations
items.statement: Definition A.1.2. For a valued field (L,|·|) and G' one of the groups above, 𝓓_{G',K} = 𝓗_{G',K} = C_c^∞(K\G'/K,L) and 𝓓_{G'} = lim_K 𝓓_{G',K}; a coadmissible G'-representation over (L,|·|) is a topological right 𝓓_{G'}-module M such that for every compact G^∘ ⊂ G' there are topological 𝓓_{G^∘,K}-modules M_K with M_K ≅ M_{K'} ⊗_{𝓓_{G^∘,K'}}𝓓_{G^∘,K} for K' ⊂ K and M ≅ lim_K M_K. For L/Q_p finite, M is p-adic locally algebraic coadmissible if it is coadmissible for the trivial norm and its restriction to G_Δ is coadmissible for the p-adic norm. The typical example is lim_{K_p}H_i(Y_{K^pK_p},𝓦) ⊗ W^∨.
items.locator: Definition A.1.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Schneider–Teitelbaum, Algebras of p-adic distributions and admissible representations, p. 152)

items.name: Hida's ordinary projector on admissible and coadmissible modules
items.statement: For Π = Π_p ⊗ W p-adic locally algebraic admissible, with Π^{N_{0,(r)}} := Π^{N_{0,(r)}} ⊗ W^N and Hecke-stable lattices, Π^{∘,N_0} is stable under U_{p∞} and e^{ord} := lim_n U_{p∞}^{n!} is a well-defined idempotent whose image Π^{∘,ord} is the maximal split O_L-submodule of Π^{∘,N_0} on which U_{p∞} acts invertibly; Π^{ord} := e^{ord}Π^{N_0}. If Π_p and W are irreducible then dim Π^{ord} ∈ {0,1}, and Π is ordinary in the second case, independently of the lattices. Dually, for a p-adic locally algebraic coadmissible right module M = M_p ⊗ W^∨ one obtains M^{(∘),ord} := M^{(∘)}_{N_0}e^{ord}. Both retain the action of the operators U_{t,p∞}.
items.locator: §A.1.3 (Ordinary parts of admissible or coadmissible G_*-modules), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)
items.note: L0a plans exactly the finite and profinite ordinary projector: the Fitting decomposition, the eventual constancy of U^{n!}, the inverse-limit construction, invertibility on the image and topological nilpotence on the complement, with exactness under the actual hypotheses.

items.name: The purely imaginary element j_v, the embedding E_v ↪ B_v, and the elements w_r, γ_r
items.statement: For v | p with ramification degree e_v, uniformiser ϖ_v with ∏_v ϖ_v^{e_v} = p, and θ_v with O_{E,v} = O_{F,v}[θ_v] in the nonsplit case: j_v := (−1_w,1_{w^c}) if E_v = E_w^× × E_{w^c}^×, and j_v := θ_v^c − θ_v if E_v is a field. The embedding E_v ↪ B_v is t ↦ diag(t_w,t_{w^c}) in the split case and a+θb ↦ ((a+b Tr_vθ_v, b Nm_vθ_v),(−b, a)) otherwise. For r ≥ 0, w_{r,v} := ((0,1),(−p^r,0)) ∈ GL_2(F_v) and γ_{r,v} := ((p^r,1),(0,1)) if v splits, ((p^r Nm_v(θ_v),0),(0,1)) if v is nonsplit, with w_r := ∏_v w_{r,v} and γ_r := ∏_v γ_{r,v}.
items.locator: §A.1.4 (Special group elements, and further notation) with display (A.1.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Anti-ordinary parts
items.statement: With w = ((0,1),(−1,0)) ∈ G_{*,Δ}, N^− := w^{−1}Nw and U^-_{p∞} := U_{w^{−1}diag(p,1)w,p∞}, the anti-ordinary part of a p-adic admissible locally algebraic Π is π^a := π_p^a ⊗ W^{N^−} ⊂ π, the ordinary part for N^− and U^-_{p∞}; since π^w ≅ π, π^a and π^{ord} have the same dimension. Dually, for coadmissible M the anti-ordinary part is the quotient M^a := M_p^a ⊗ W_{N^−}.
items.locator: §A.2.1 (Ordinary and anti-ordinary parts), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The Atkin–Lehner-type operator from ordinary to anti-ordinary parts
items.statement: Proposition A.2.1. For an algebraic W of G_∞: (1) for a p-adic locally algebraic admissible π there is an isomorphism w_a^{ord} : π^{ord} → π^a, f ↦ lim_r p^{r[F:Q]}w_{r,p}w_{0,∞}^ι U_p^{−r}f, the sequence being constant as soon as f_p ∈ π_p^{U^1_1(p^r)}; (2) for a coadmissible M there is a map w_a^{ord} : M^{ord} → M^a, m_p ⊗ m_∞ ↦ lim_r p^{r[F:Q]}[m U_p^{−r}w_{r,p}]_{N_0^−} ⊗ [m_∞w_{0,∞}^ι]_{N^−}. Its local components w^{ord}_{a,v} : π_v^{ord} → π_v^a and w^{ord}_{a,v,∞} : W_v^{N_v} → W_v^{N_v^−} are defined in the same way.
items.locator: Proposition A.2.1 with display (A.2.1), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Nondegeneracy of the ordinary pairing
items.statement: Lemma A.2.2. For an ordinary representation π of G and a nondegenerate G-invariant (,) : π ⊗ π^∨ → L, the pairing (f_1,f_2)^{ord} := (w_a^{ord}f_1,f_2) on π^{ord} ⊗ π^{∨,ord} is nondegenerate.
items.locator: Lemma A.2.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The Hecke-algebra identity behind the toric-to-ordinary operator
items.statement: Lemma A.2.3. For all r ≥ 1 there is an identity of Hecke operators for (G×H)'_v: V'_{v,r+1}(Σ_{t ∈ V'_{v,r}/V'_{v,r+1}}t)·γ_{r+1,v}K_{v,r} = V'_{v,r+1}γ_{r,v}·U_{ϖ_v}K_{v,r}.
items.locator: Lemma A.2.3, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The semilocal operator γ^{ord}_{H'} intertwining ordinary and toric parts
items.statement: Proposition A.2.4. Let W be an algebraic representation of (G×H)'_∞ of the shape W_σ = Sym^{k_σ−2}Std·det^{(w−k_σ+2)/2} ⊗ σ^{(l_σ−w)/2}(σ^c)^{(−l_σ−w)/2}, and set c(W_σ) := j_v^{−w−k_σ+2}·binom(k_σ−2,(k_σ−2−l_σ)/2)·(1 if v splits, θ^{c,(k−2−l)/2}θ^{(k−2+l)/2} otherwise), c(W) := ∏_σ c(W_σ). (1) For a p-adic locally algebraic admissible Π = Π_p ⊗ W of (G×H)' there is a map γ^{ord}_{H'} : Π^{ord} → Π_{H'}, f ↦ lim_r H'[p^{r[F:Q]}c(W)^{−1}γ_{r,p∞}U_{p∞}^{−r}f], the sequence being constant once f_p ∈ Π^{K_{p,r}}. (2) For a coadmissible M = M_p ⊗ W^∨ there is γ^{ord}_{H'} : M^{H'} → M^{ord}, m ↦ lim_r [p^{r[F:Q]}c(W)^{−1}m γ_{r,p∞}]_{N_{0,r}}e^{ord}U_{p∞}^{−r}. The local components γ^{ord}_{H',v} and γ^{ord}_{H',v,∞} are defined in the same way.
items.locator: Proposition A.2.4 with displays (A.2.2)–(A.2.4), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: γ^{ord}_{H'} annihilates exactly the exceptional representations
items.statement: Lemma A.2.5. For an ordinary, distinguished, irreducible representation Π = π ⊗ χ of (G×H)' the following are equivalent: Π is exceptional; e_v(V_{(π,χ)}) = 0; there is a nonzero P ∈ Π^{*,H'} with P^{ord} := Pγ^{ord}_{H'} = 0; P^{ord} = 0 for every P ∈ Π^{*,H'}.
items.locator: Lemma A.2.5 with §A.2.3, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The Tate integral as an inverse gamma factor
items.statement: Lemma A.3.1. For characters μ : F_v^× → C^× and ψ : F_v → C^× with ψ ≠ 1, and a Haar measure d^×y on F_v^×, ∫_{F_v^×}μ(y)ψ(y)d^×y = (d^×y/d^×_ψy)·μ(−1)·γ(μ,ψ)^{−1}, where d_ψ y is the selfdual measure and d^×_ψ y = d_ψ y/|y|.
items.locator: Lemma A.3.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024) (Disegni, nonsplit primes, Lemma A.1.1; Tate's thesis)
items.note: AL.1 plans Tate's local zeta integrals with their functional equation, gamma factors and selfdual measures; this identity is the evaluation of such an integral.

items.name: Refined representations and their ordinary lines
items.statement: Definition A.3.2. A refined representation (π,α) of G_v over L is a smooth irreducible infinite-dimensional π together with a character α : F_v^× → L^× such that π embeds into the un-normalised induction Ind(|·|α, |·|^{−1}ωα^{−1}) for some central character ω; π admits a refinement iff it is neither supercuspidal nor one-dimensional. A refined Π = π ⊗ χ of (G×H)'_v requires ωχ|_{F_v^×} = 1. Then π^{ord} ⊂ π^{N_0} is the line on which U_t acts by α(t), Π^{ord} := π^{ord} ⊗ χ, and the attached Weil–Deligne representation has a unique filtration 0 → V_π^+ → V_π → V_π^− → 0 with WD_{F_v} acting on V_π^+ through α|·|. The ordinary pairing is (f,f^∨)^{ord}_π := (w_a^{ord}f,f^∨).
items.locator: Definition A.3.2 with §A.3.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The local ordinary pairing as an adjoint gamma factor
items.statement: Lemma A.3.3. Let (π,α) be a refined representation of G_p over C with central character ω, α^∨ = αω^{−1}, ad(V_π)^{++}(1) = Hom(V_π^−,V_π^+)(1). Fix ψ of level 0 and Kirillov models of ιπ_v and π_v^∨ for ψ_v, −ψ_v; let f_v^{(∨)}(y) := 1_{O_{F,v}}(y)α_v^{(∨)}|·|_v(y) ∈ π_v^{ord}, and let (,)_{π,v} be the Kirillov pairing ∫_{F^×}f(y)f^∨(y)d^×_ψ y. Then (f,f^∨)^{ord}_{π,v} = ω_v(−1)·γ(ad(V_π)^{++}(1),ψ)^{−1}.
items.locator: Lemma A.3.3 with displays (A.3.1)–(A.3.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The local toric period of the ordinary vectors and the factor e_v
items.statement: Proposition A.3.4. Let Π = π ⊗ χ be a refined representation of (G×H)'_v over L with Weil–Deligne representation V = V_{π|WD_{E_v}} ⊗ χ, and γ^{ord}_{H'} = γ^{ord}_{H',v}. Then Q_{dt}(γ^{ord}_{H'}f_1 ⊗ γ^{ord}_{H'}f_2 / w_a^{ord}f_3 ⊗ f_4) = e_v(V_{(π,χ)})·Q^{ord}_{dt}(f_1⊗f_2/f_3⊗f_4), where e_v(V_{(π,χ)}) = 𝓛(V_{(π,χ)},0)^{−1}·ι^{−1}(|d|_v^{−1/2}γ(ad(ιV_π^{++})(1),ψ_v)·∏_{w|v}γ(ιV^+_{|WD_{E_w}},ψ_{E_w})^{−1}), independently of ι : L ↪ C and of ψ.
items.locator: Proposition A.3.4, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Polynomial models and the invariant pairing on the algebraic weight
items.statement: §A.4.1. The representation W of (G×H)'_{v,∞} is identified with the homogeneous polynomials p(x,y) of degree k−2 over L, the action being p.(g,h)(x,y) = det(g)^{(w−k+2)/2}σ(h)^{(l−w)/2}σ^c(h)^{(−l−w)/2}p(g(x,y)^T) on the right and the transposed formula on the left, and the fixed invariant pairing is (x^{k−2−a}y^a, x^{a'}y^{k−2−a'}) = (−1)^a binom(k−2,a)^{−1}δ_{a,a'}. With respect to this model the bounded denominator of the invariant pairing is |W| = ord_p binom(k−2,(k−2+l)/2).
items.locator: §A.4.1 with displays (A.4.1)–(A.4.2), Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The archimedean value of the operator w_a^{ord}
items.statement: Lemma A.4.1. For W as above viewed as a left representation of G_{v,∞} only, W^N is spanned by x^{k−2}, W_N by the image of y^{k−2}, and (w_a^{ord}(x^{k−2}),x^{k−2}) = 1.
items.locator: Lemma A.4.1, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: Unitarity of the algebraic part of γ^{ord}_{H'}
items.statement: Lemma A.4.2. For a decomposition M_p = M_{p,0} ⊗ W_p of a locally algebraic coadmissible right (G×H)'_p-representation and the corresponding factorisation γ^{ord}_{H'} = lim_r (p^{r[F:Q]}γ_{r,p}U_p^{−r}) ⊗ γ_{r,p}U_p^{−r} ⊗ c(W)^{−1}γ^ι_{0,∞}, the operator ^{alg}γ^{ord}_{H'} := lim_r γ_{r,p}U_p^{−r} ⊗ c(W)^{−1}γ^ι_{0,∞} : W^{H'} ⊗ W^{∨,H'} → W^N ⊗ W_N is unitary: for any invariant pairing on W ⊗ W^∨ and ξ ∈ W^{H'}, ξ^∨ ∈ W^{∨,H'}, the images of ξ ⊗ ξ^∨ and of ^{alg}γ^{ord}_{H'}(ξ ⊗ ξ^∨) under the induced pairings coincide. This is what justifies the constant c(W) and what proves Proposition 6.3.2.
items.locator: Lemma A.4.2 with §A.4.2, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

items.name: The archimedean comparison of the toric pairing and its ordinary variant
items.statement: Proposition A.4.3. For a representation W of (G×H)'_{v,∞} over L and all f_1,f_3 ∈ W^N, f_2,f_4 ∈ W^{∨,N} with f_3,f_4 ≠ 0, Q_{dt}(γ^{ord}_{H'}f_1 ⊗ γ^{ord}_{H'}f_2 / w_a^{ord}f_3 ⊗ f_4) = dim W · Q^{ord}_{dt}(f_1⊗f_2/f_3⊗f_4).
items.locator: Proposition A.4.3, Disegni, arXiv:2001.00045v4 (23 February 2024)

prerequisites.citation: Daniel Disegni, "The p-adic Gross–Zagier formula on Shimura curves, II: nonsplit primes", J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 22 (2023), no. 5, 2199–2240
prerequisites.why: Theorem B of this paper in the trivial-weight case is the input from which everything else is interpolated; Theorem A of that paper is the one-variable p-adic L-function compared in Lemma 7.1.3. The correction to that paper is the sole reason for Appendix B of the present one, so its corrected statement — the formula for ordinary, locally distinguished, potentially crystalline, non-exceptional Π of trivial weight satisfying (★) — must be established before any of Theorems A, B, B^ord, D and E can be planned.

prerequisites.citation: Daniel Disegni, "The p-adic Gross–Zagier formula on Shimura curves", Compos. Math. 153 (2017), no. 10, 1987–2074
prerequisites.why: The split-prime half of the same trivial-weight input, together with the conventions for the automorphic inner product, the local toric integrals and the comparison of p-adic height pairings on abelian varieties that the present paper reuses without reproving.

prerequisites.citation: Daniel Disegni, "p-adic L-functions via local-global interpolation: the case of GL_2 × GU(1)", Canad. J. Math. 75 (2023), no. 4, 1010–1046
prerequisites.why: Theorem 1.4.1, the two-variable p-adic L-function 𝓛_p(𝓥^♯) with its interpolation property, is quoted from this paper; the entire right-hand side of Theorems D and H is that function, and its uniqueness characterisation fixes all the normalisations.

Sections 3–4 supply continuous cochains of ind-admissible modules, §11.1 the p-adic height pairing, and Theorem 12.2.3 the parity theorem used in §7.3.4. Section 5 of the present paper is an extension of this theory to sheaves over an eigenvariety and cannot be planned without it.

prerequisites.citation: Rodolfo Venerucci, "p-adic regulators and p-adic families of modular forms", Thesis, Università di Milano (2012), Appendix C
prerequisites.why: Lemma 0.16 gives the specialisation of the height pairing at a regular point and §0.21 constructs the height pairing valued in the conormal sheaf of a local complete intersection; Proposition 5.3.4 and hence the whole formulation of Theorem D depend on it.

prerequisites.citation: Olivier Fouquet, "Dihedral Iwasawa theory of nearly ordinary quaternionic automorphic forms", Compos. Math. 149 (2013), no. 3, 356–416
prerequisites.why: Theorem B(i) and B(iii) are the Euler-system bounds used in Theorem A(2) and Theorem E; the hypotheses of that theorem are carried verbatim into the statements here and are not reproved.

prerequisites.citation: Haruzo Hida, "Control of nearly ordinary Hecke algebras", preprint (2009); and "On p-adic Hecke algebras for GL_2 over totally real fields", Ann. of Math. (2) 128 (1988), 295–384
prerequisites.why: Theorem 1.2 of the first and §8 of the second give the freeness and control theorems quoted as Proposition 3.1.2 for G; the whole of §3.1 rests on them.

prerequisites.citation: Daniel Disegni, "Local Langlands correspondence, local factors, and zeta integrals in analytic families", J. Lond. Math. Soc. (2) 101 (2020), 735–764
prerequisites.why: Theorem 3.2.1 (the map to the Bernstein variety) and Theorem 4.4.3 (recognition of a family from its fibres) are what make Lemma 3.3.3 and Theorem 3.3.10 possible, and the co-Whittaker formalism fixes the normalisations of the interpolated local factors in §4.4.

prerequisites.citation: Henri Carayol, "Sur les représentations l-adiques associées aux formes modulaires de Hilbert", Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. (4) 19 (1986), 409–468; and "Sur la mauvaise réduction des courbes de Shimura", Compositio Math. 59 (1986), 151–230
prerequisites.why: The construction of the Galois representations of Hilbert modular forms, local–global compatibility away from p, and the isotypic decomposition of the homology of the quaternionic tower (Proposition 2.5.2), together with the neatness lemma quoted as Lemma 2.3.1.

prerequisites.citation: J.-L. Waldspurger, "Sur les valeurs de certaines fonctions L automorphes en leur centre de symétrie", Compositio Math. 54 (1985), 173–242
prerequisites.why: Lemme 10 and Lemme 14 are used directly (the local dichotomy in Lemma 6.4.6 and the unramified toric value in Lemma 4.2.1), and the classical formula is the input to Theorem H.

prerequisites.citation: Benjamin Howard, "Variation of Heegner points in Hida families", Invent. Math. 167 (2007), 91–128
prerequisites.why: The proof of Proposition 2.4.5 at the primes above p is quoted verbatim in the proof of Lemma 6.4.4, and Theorem C answers the question Howard raises about the interpolation of Heegner cycles.

prerequisites.citation: Nicholas M. Katz, "p-adic L-functions for CM fields", Invent. Math. 49 (1978), 199–297, with Hida–Tilouine, Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. 26 (1993), 189–259
prerequisites.why: The Katz p-adic L-function attached to a p-adic CM type, its interpolation range and the uniqueness of the CM type containing a given self-dual point are the backbone of the proof of Theorem F.

prerequisites.citation: Haruzo Hida, "Anticyclotomic main conjectures", Doc. Math. Extra Vol. (2006), 465–532, and "Quadratic exercises in Iwasawa theory", Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2009, 912–952; Ming-Lun Hsieh, J. Reine Angew. Math. 688 (2014), 67–100; Ashay Burungale, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 14 (2015), 131–148; Ashay Burungale and Daniel Disegni, Ann. Inst. Fourier 70 (2020), 2077–2101
prerequisites.why: The four inputs of the proof of Theorem F: the anticyclotomic main conjecture on a suitable component, the non-vanishing of the anticyclotomic Katz L-function, the non-vanishing of the normal derivative of the Katz L-function, and the sign-change lemma producing a component of type +1.

prerequisites.citation: Massimo Bertolini and Henri Darmon, "A rigid analytic Gross–Zagier formula and arithmetic applications", Ann. of Math. (2) 146 (1997), 111–147, with their survey "The p-adic L-functions of modular elliptic curves" (2001), Theorem 5.4
prerequisites.why: The exceptional-zero evaluation of the Heegner class at the elliptic-curve point that drives the whole proof of Theorem G and the new proof of Greenberg–Stevens in Remark 7.3.4.

prerequisites.citation: Michele Fornea and Lennart Gehrmann, "Plectic Stark–Heegner points", arXiv:2104.12575; Michele Fornea, Xavier Guitart and Marc Masdeu, "Plectic p-adic invariants", arXiv:2104.12566
prerequisites.why: Theorem A of the first and Conjectures 1.3, 1.5 of the second are the higher-rank evidence for Conjecture Pf discussed in §7.3.5; the comparison there is an equivalence conditional on those conjectures, not a proof of either.

prerequisites.citation: Peter Schneider and Jeremy Teitelbaum, "Algebras of p-adic distributions and admissible representations", Invent. Math. 153 (2003), 145–196
prerequisites.why: The notion of coadmissible module over the distribution algebra, on which Definition A.1.2 and the whole treatment of completed homology as a coadmissible representation are modelled.

prerequisites.citation: Raphaël Rouquier, "Caractérisation des caractères et pseudo-caractères", J. Algebra 180 (1996), 571–586; David J. Saltman, "Lectures on division algebras", CBMS 94 (1999); Max-Albert Knus and Manuel Ojanguren, "Théorie de la descente et algèbres d'Azumaya", LNM 389 (1974); Gaëtan Chenevier, J. Reine Angew. Math. 570 (2004), 143–217
prerequisites.why: Théorème 5.1, Corollary 2.9, the local innerness of automorphisms of Azumaya algebras and the openness of the irreducibility locus are the four ingredients of Lemmas 3.2.1–3.2.2, which supply the family Galois representation in the residually reducible case.

routes.title: Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights, Part II: universal p-adic Gross–Zagier formulas over Hida families
routes.brief:
Disegni, Invent. math. 230 (2022), 509-649, proves the p-adic Gross-Zagier formula for Hilbert modular forms of arbitrary cohomological weight twisted by Hecke characters of a CM extension, and interpolates it into a single identity over a Hida family for (G x H)'. GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights plans the complex Gross-Zagier and Waldspurger formulas (GZ.5, GZ.8) and one p-adic statement only, the split ordinary logarithm/toric formula of GZ.9, which explicitly refuses to be identified with a p-adic height derivative formula and excludes the exceptional-zero case; so the p-adic height side, its universal form and its exceptional-zero branch are new work in that roadmap's direction.

Import, never re-plan:
- GZ.0 for normalisations and GZ.3-GZ.5 for the Hodge class, the rational automorphic realisations, Saito-Tunnell multiplicity one, the normalised local toric integrals and the Waldspurger formula;
- SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights, the Part II of SelmerIwasawaCohomology proposed by PAPER-DISEGNI-LIU-24 and extended by this extraction, for Nekovar's Selmer complexes over a base and the height pairings;
- PadicFamilies L0/L0a/L4/L5 for Hida theory and the big Galois representation, AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.2-R19.6 for the Galois representations of Hilbert modular forms, HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.1-R18.4 for the quaternionic towers and their cohomology, GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16-R17 for local Langlands and Jacquet-Langlands, AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0-L3h for the p-adic L-functions, GeneralizedHeegnerCycles GH.1 for the etale Abel-Jacobi map, HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.8 for the Euler-system bounds.

Construct: incoherent reductive groups and their Shimura towers in Emerton's p-adic formulation; the Heegner cycles with coefficients in an automorphic local system and the functionals P_Pi; the sheaves V, V_w^{pm} and the universal ordinary representation over a locally distinguished Hida family, with the local-global compatibility of Theorem 3.3.10 and the skew-hermitian dualities of Proposition 4.1.7; the semilocal operators w_a^{ord} and gamma_{H'}^{ord} of Appendix A with the local toric period computation in terms of gamma factors (Proposition A.3.4), which is the technical heart; the interpolated toric functional Q (Theorem 4.4.3); the universal Heegner class and its Selmer property (Theorem C); the Pfaffian regulators and Conjecture Pf of section 7.3 with the Fornea-Gehrmann comparison.

The final theorems are Theorem B (the p-adic Gross-Zagier formula for arbitrary weight, under condition (star) of the Correction), Theorem D (the universal formula over a Hida* family), Theorem A (the p-adic Beilinson-Bloch-Kato conjecture in analytic rank one), Theorem E (an Iwasawa main conjecture for derivatives), Theorems F and G (non-vanishing of p-adic heights), Theorem H (the universal Waldspurger formula) and the new proof of Greenberg-Stevens in Remark 7.3.4. Every statement must carry the corrected hypotheses of Appendix B: condition (star) for Theorems A, B and B^{ord}, and Hida* families for D and E.
routes.reason: GZ.8 proves the complex Gross–Zagier formula and GZ.9 the split ordinary p-adic logarithm/toric formula, which its own description forbids identifying with a p-adic height derivative formula and which excludes the exceptional-zero case. The p-adic height side of the formula, its extension to arbitrary cohomological weight and to CM extensions of a totally real field, its interpolation over a Hida family, and the Bertolini–Darmon exceptional-zero branch are therefore new layers in the direction of GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights, not a re-planning of it.

routes.title: Selmer groups, continuous integral cohomology, and Iwasawa cohomology, Part II: p-adic height pairings and bi-extensions of cycles
routes.brief:
PAPER-DISEGNI-LIU-24 proposed this Part II for Nekovar's p-adic height pairing and the bi-extensions of algebraic cycles of Appendices A-B of Disegni-Liu, Invent. math. 236 (2024), 219-371. This extraction reuses that candidate and adds the part of Nekovar's theory that varies in families, which section 5 of the present paper sets up and which SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0-L4 does not plan: L2 constructs the Selmer complex as a mapping fibre for a lattice T over a p-adic ring, not for a sheaf over a base.

Section 5 of the present paper is the family version of the same theory — continuous cohomology of ind-admissible sheaves over the category of open subschemes of Spec R°, Greenberg data and Selmer complexes over a base, and Venerucci's conormal-valued height pairing — which SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2 does not plan, since it works with a single lattice T over a p-adic ring.

L0 plans ordinary Hecke algebras and their finite flatness, L5 the Hida control theorem on the integral Hilbert automorphic modules over totally real fields, and L4 the ordinary big Galois representation with its local ordinary filtration, saturation and arithmetic specialisation. This source adds, in that setting: the weight space of an arbitrary one of the five groups G, H, G×H, (G×H)', H' with the Leopoldt defect in its dimension formula; the ordinary completed homology of the quaternionic tower and the Künneth-plus-quotient step producing the projective Λ_{(G×H)'}-module M_{(G×H)',K^p}; the ordinary eigenvariety with its classical ind-subscheme, the étaleness of the weight map at classical points and the resulting regularity; the identification of the fibres of the sheaf 𝓜 with the ordinary parts of the corresponding automorphic representations, including the vanishing of the central character over the quotient group; the completed group algebra description of the abelian eigenvariety for H with its universal character; the constancy of the conductor along a component and the descent of a component to its new level; Schur's lemma for the family representation; and, most importantly, the construction of the ordinary filtration 0 → 𝓥^+_v → 𝓥_v → 𝓥^−_v → 0 over a Hida family with no hypothesis on the residual representation, which L4's statement obtains only when the residual hypotheses justify passing from a pseudorepresentation to a representation.

R19.6 plans the determinant law built from Hecke operators and Frobenius polynomials and its representability over a localised completed Hecke algebra under absolute residual irreducibility. This source adds the geometric form used over an eigenvariety: over an integral scheme, an irreducible pseudocharacter has an open irreducibility locus, the quotient O_X[G]/Ker(𝓣) is Azumaya of rank n², the natural maps to the endomorphism algebras of any two representations with that trace are isomorphisms, and hence any two such representations differ by a twist by a line bundle with trivial Galois action. The underlying Azumaya statement — an isomorphism of endomorphism algebras of two vector bundles is inner up to a line bundle, because automorphisms of an Azumaya algebra are Zariski-locally inner — is also not in the atlas; Tau Ceti's Skolem–Noether theorem is the field case only.

R16.2 plans local smooth representation theory and R16.3 local Langlands for GL₂, and SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.5 plans Helm's integral co-Whittaker families for ℓ ≠ p. This source adds the analytic-families correspondence of Disegni's J. Lond. Math. Soc. paper, which is what the present paper actually uses and which is a different theorem from Helm's: to a rank-two family of Weil–Deligne representations over a Noetherian Q-scheme it attaches a co-Whittaker family of smooth GL₂(F)-representations, with the map to the Bernstein variety of supercuspidal supports and the recognition theorem identifying, up to a line bundle over an open subset, any smooth admissible family with the right fibres on a dense set. The paper's Lemma 3.3.3 — a single compact open subgroup of the ramified quaternionic group fixes every classical member of a Hida family — is the application of that correspondence to the three possible inertial classes.

L0 plans ray-class character spaces, locally algebraic Hecke characters and the conditional construction principle for a distribution interpolating period-normalised algebraic values; L1 the cohomological GL₂/F input; L5 the comparison of periods and conventions and the statement of the Coates–Perrin-Riou/Panchishkin problem. This source supplies a worked instance of exactly that shape which the atlas does not otherwise plan: the two-variable p-adic L-function 𝓛_p(𝓥^♯) on the ordinary eigenvariety for G₀ × H over a totally real field, with its precise interpolation formula e_{p∞}(V_{(π,χ)})·𝓛(V_{(π,χ)},0) over the explicit critical range, the polar locus disjoint from the classical points, the full list of local factors 𝓛(V_{(π,χ),v},0) and of inverse Deligne–Langlands gamma factors entering e_v and e_∞, the cyclotomic space Γ_F with its Leopoldt-sensitive dimension, the restriction defining 𝓛_p(V_{(π₀,χ)},s) and its derivative, and the comparison of that restriction at a point of trivial weight with the one-variable p-adic L-function of a modular abelian variety. It also adds the non-vanishing of the normal derivative of Katz's p-adic L-function along the self-dual subvariety, which L3 constructs but whose derivative it does not study.

HE.8 plans the anticyclotomic Heegner classes over Q, Howard's divisibility and the BCGS comparison. This source adds Fouquet's dihedral Iwasawa theory of nearly ordinary quaternionic automorphic forms over a totally real field, whose Theorem B(i) and B(iii) are the Euler-system inputs of Theorem A(2) and Theorem E of this paper: a one-dimensional Selmer group and a bound on the characteristic ideal of the torsion of H̃²_f, at finite level and in the two-variable family, under hypotheses stated on the residual representation and the ramification. Nothing in HE.8 currently covers the totally real, nearly ordinary, quaternionic case, and these bounds are quoted, not proved, in the present paper.

L6 is the milestone that exposes the separately owned main-conjecture branches through a common interface and names their proof owners. This source adds the branch that Theorem F of this paper consumes and that L6's table does not list: the anticyclotomic main conjecture for self-dual Hecke characters of a CM field over a totally real field, in Hida's form, on a component of the self-dual character space satisfying his hypotheses, together with the sign-change argument of Burungale–Disegni that moves from a component of type −1 to a component of type +1 still satisfying those hypotheses, and the identification of an anticyclotomic character as χ₀^c χ₀^{−1}. The equivalence used is between the non-vanishing of the Katz L-function at a classical point and the vanishing of the Bloch–Kato Selmer group of the corresponding character.

GZ.4 plans the normalised toric matrix-coefficient integrals with their convergence, rationality and unramified value, and GZ.5 the coherent theta kernels and the Waldspurger formula with its adjoint L-value and zeta/eta factors. This source adds the three local computations the present paper needs in that same layer: the exact normalising factor 𝓛(V_{(π,χ),v},0) = ζ_{F,v}(2)L(V_v,0)/(L(1,η_v)L(ad(V_{π,v}),1)), with its archimedean variant, written as the local factor of a virtual motive; the identification, when E_v = F_v ⊕ F_v, of the normalised toric integral with a product of two GL₂ × GL₁ zeta integrals in Kirillov models; and the value of the toric pairing on the line of H'-invariants when B_v is nonsplit, where the integral degenerates to 𝓛(V_{(π,χ),v},0)^{−1} vol(E_v^×/F_v^×) times the invariant pairing. These are local statements about the same object GZ.4 owns, not new layers.
